> - Drop the `Supersede` decision and `workflow_delta_from_base` entirely (schema v1 → v2 `ReleasePrSnapshot`/`Action`/`Decision` types) — no replacement, no runtime fallback — since it only masked the token-permission problem by cutting a fresh SHA-suffixed PR whenever workflow files drifted on `main`.
> - Add supporting building blocks: `ReleasePrCommitPlanV1::from_changes` (fails closed on workflow paths, non-regular file modes, renames, and oversized payloads), `ShellGit::staged_changes_since`, and a new `callisto release-pr commit-plan` CLI subcommand.
>
> ## Why
> On a public repo, the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot write `.github/workflows/*` through the Git push protocol — confirmed by a real production failure (GitHub Actions run 33679599559 on orin-dx/callisto, 2026-09-02): `refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow '.github/workflows/callisto-ci.yml' without 'workflows' permission`. The prior mitigation (`Supersede`: close the stale PR, open a fresh SHA-suffixed one) worked around the symptom and produced unwanted churn (PR #28 closed, #48 opened) every time a workflow file moved.
>

> ## Breaking Changes

content.text:
Found it — and this confirms my earlier answer was wrong for a different reason than I said, so let me be precise about what actually happened.

**The merge commit itself is unsigned:**
```json
{"author":"github-actions[bot]","committer":"Gabe Castro","parents":["a1f1ebcc..."],"reason":"unsigned","verified":false}
```

One parent (a squash/rebase-style commit, not a two-parent merge), and the **committer is your own identity, not GitHub's**. That's the signature of a merge done by pushing locally (checkout, merge/rebase, `git push`) rather than through GitHub's own merge button or `gh pr merge` — a commit GitHub itself creates server-side always comes back signed and verified, regardless of merge strategy.

The `release-candidate` job correctly found PR #48 as the merged, matching release PR (that part passed — `prs == 1`), but its second, deliberate check failed: `verified == true`. Its own code comment states the intent directly: *"a trusted merge must be both an actual merge of the managed PR and a GitHub-verified signed commit. It cannot be a direct push."* That's a real trust boundary from the release-trust spec work, not a bug — it's specifically designed to reject exactly this: someone locally pushing something onto `main` that merely looks like the release PR's merge, bypassing GitHub's own record of the merge event. So `plan`/`build`/`execute` correctly stayed skipped.

**Net effect:** the version bump content is already on `main` (0.5.0 → 0.6.0 across 10 packages), but no tag, no GitHub release, no crates.io/npm publish happened, and this specific commit will never trigger one — branch protection on `main` doesn't require signed commits, so nothing stopped the push, but the pipeline's own provenance gate did.

This isn't something I can silently fix — you have a real decision to make. A couple of paths, not a recommendation yet:
1. Since PR #48 is already closed/merged, you can't re-merge it through GitHub's UI/API to get a signed commit after the fact.
2. You could publish this version manually/locally using `callisto release execute` outside the gated pipeline (bypasses the whole point of the trust boundary — probably not what you want).
3. Treat this as a one-off skip and let the next real changeset cycle produce a fresh release PR that *is* merged through GitHub's merge button/API next time.

How do you want to handle it?

You clicked the merge button, genuinely. The real cause is that **"Rebase and merge" was the strategy used (or selected as default), and GitHub does not cryptographically sign rebase-merge commits** the way it signs squash and merge-commit strategies — it replays the PR's own existing commit onto `main` with a new parent rather than authoring a fresh, GitHub-signed commit on your behalf. Technically yes — but I'd want to be direct about what you'd be giving up before touching it.

The `verified == true` check exists specifically to rule out a scenario the PR-association check alone doesn't fully close: a token or bot with `contents: write` on `main` pushing a commit directly (bypassing PR review entirely) that happens to superficially match the merged-PR pattern. Only GitHub's own merge/squash mechanism produces a signature it can verify — that's the actual thing distinguishing "a real review-then-merge happened" from "someone with push access manufactured matching content." Removing the check means: from now on, *any* push to `main` matching the branch-name pattern can trigger a real crates.io/npm publish, regardless of whether it went through review at all.

The thing is — you don't actually need to weaken it permanently to solve today's problem. Now that rebase-merge is disabled, every future legitimate squash-merge *will* come back signed, so the check will never produce another false negative like this one going forward. It only matters for this one already-merged, unsigned commit.

Two better-scoped options than a blanket removal:

1. **Revert-and-redo** (what I described before) — no pipeline change at all, just gets a fresh signed merge for the same content.
2. **A one-time, explicit manual override**: add a `workflow_dispatch` input to the Durable release workflow (e.g. `override_commit`) that lets a human explicitly assert "treat this specific commit as the release candidate," bypassing the signature check *only* when a person deliberately typed that SHA in — not a standing weakening of the default push-triggered path. This is a real (small) code/spec change, not a config toggle, so it'd need its own review too.

If you want speed over process, (2) is faster to use today but is a permanent addition to the codebase (once built, it stays); (1) touches nothing but takes an extra PR cycle. Which way do you want to go?

Good point, and that changes the calculus — this isn't just about our own repo's merge settings anymore, it's about what the action can promise to *every* repo that uses it. Not every consumer can guarantee GitHub-signed merges (some don't use squash-only, some route merges through third-party merge-queue tools that don't produce GitHub's own signature, some organizations disable it entirely).

Given that, I don't think the right fix is removing the check — it's making it **configurable per-repo** rather than hardcoded: a new action input (e.g. `require_verified_merge_commit`, defaulting to `true`) that a repo can explicitly opt out of if it can't guarantee signed merges, with the PR-association check (`prs == 1`, base/head match) remaining mandatory either way as the floor. Default stays strict for repos like ours that can meet it; repos that can't, opt out with eyes open to the reduced provenance guarantee, documented plainly in the spec so it's a deliberate choice, not a silent gap.

That's a real trust-boundary change across `SPEC-RELEASE-INTERFACES-013`/`SPEC-RELEASE-TRUST-010`, not a quick toggle — it needs the same rigor as everything else here (spec update, action input, tests for both branches of the flag). Worth scoping as its own piece of work separate from fixing today's stuck release.

content.text:
Fair, and re-judging against that bar changes things a lot — most of these names actually pull real weight once you look closely (each word maps to an actual technical/security property), and I was wrong to flatten them:

- "ephemeral intent" — tells you intent is never persisted/cached, a real property from the spec.
- "intent-bound source tree" — tells you the build is deterministically tied to a specific verified intent, not built from arbitrary state.
- "verify same-run handoff *before credentials*" — tells you the ordering guarantee (handoff verified before secrets become available).
- "attest *declared* binary artifacts" — specific about what gets attested vs. what doesn't.
- "verify environment protection" / "require environment reviewers" — literally names the GitHub feature being checked.

None of that is filler — cutting it would make the Actions UI less informative, not cleaner. That's the opposite of what you asked for.

The one that's actually empty is the top-level workflow title: **"Durable release"**. "Durable" is a quality claim, not a description of what happens — it doesn't tell a reader anything the job names below it don't already say better. That's the real AI-slop instance here: an abstract-sounding adjective standing in for saying anything concrete.

Revised, much narrower proposal: rename just the workflow itself, `Durable release` → `Release` (matching the plain, concrete style of the sibling `Callisto CI & Validation` workflow and the file's own name, `callisto-release.yml`). Leave every job and step name as-is.

content.text:
Correction — I was wrong to call it meaningless. There IS a real contrast: it's defined across `SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001A/B/C` and `PLAN-RELEASE-REARCHITECTURE-008-013`. The **non-durable** version is the workflow's own prior design: a single job that computed the release plan *inline*, in the same shell block that pushed tags and published — the plan lived only as an in-memory/shell-variable value for one step and was gone the instant that step ended, with no way for a human to review it before it took effect.

"Durable" specifically means: the release intent is captured as an explicit, persisted, versioned artifact that survives the boundary between an *unprivileged* plan job and a *privileged* execute job — that's literally what makes the human-approval gate (the `environment: release` reviewer step) possible at all. If the plan were computed inline like before, there'd be nothing concrete to review or gate; it'd already be done.

So it's real, deliberately chosen, and documented — just documented in the specs, not anywhere a reader glancing at the GitHub Actions tab would ever see it. That's a different problem than "meaningless jargon": it's a real term of art used with zero on-the-spot explanation in its only user-facing appearance.

Given that, I'd still rename the *workflow title* to `Release` — a one-line UI label has no room to carry that nuance regardless of whether the concept is real, and "durable" alone reads as an unexplained adjective there. But I'd leave every actual mention of "durable" in the specs/docs alone, since that's exactly where the term is properly defined and where it's doing real work. Same call as before, just for the right reason this time — want me to make that one rename?

content.text:
Approach this as the design lead at a small studio known for their versatility, giving every client a visual identity pitched at the treatment the task actually calls for. Make deliberate choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this subject, and avoid templated designs.

## Read the request first

Calibrate treatment, not whether to design. A doc deserves the same craft as a landing page - what changes is the treatment that craft is delivered in. Format is not part of this read: author HTML, and publish Markdown only when a loaded skill explicitly instructs it - a Markdown publish keeps its filename as its title and takes almost none of the craft below, and is never a way to save time.

Many requests call for a more utilitarian treatment: a plan, a memo, a demo. Make it polished: include real typographic hierarchy, considered spacing, and a proper palette, but avoid over-designing. Most pages do not need a flashy, gigantic hero. Keep flourishes tasteful and limited.

Some requests call for an editorial treatment: a landing page, a game, an app or tool they'll keep or share.

When unsure: a well-composed page is never the wrong answer; an over-designed visual identity sometimes is.

Fundamentals below apply to everything. The editorial process after that runs only when the read above says so.

## Fundamentals for every artifact

**Honor what's already there** Look for an existing design system first - CLAUDE.md, a tokens or theme file, existing component styles. When one exists, apply it; everything below fills gaps and never overrides. Precedence is always: the user's own words, then the project's existing system, then your choices.

**Ground it in the subject.** If the subject isn't already clear, pin it: one concrete subject, its audience, and the page's single job. The subject's own world - its materials, instruments, vernacular - is where distinctive choices come from. Whatever the treatment, carry at least one detail only this subject would have - its real units and scales, its document conventions, its terms of art - as content, not ornament; it costs a plain page nothing. Build with real content throughout, never lorem.

**Pair typefaces** Typography carries the page even when the page isn't about typography. Google Fonts is the one font host the Artifact CSP admits - link it directly (`<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=...&display=swap">`); a face from anywhere else must be inlined as a @font-face data URI or it falls back silently. Either way, declare a real fallback stack. Keep running text near 65 characters wide; set a type scale and stay on it; give headings `text-wrap: balance`, body text room to breathe, and uppercase labels a touch of letter-spacing.

**Load libraries, don't paste them.** When the page genuinely needs a library - React, a charting or highlighting package - load its UMD build from cdnjs (only the script - a library's stylesheet still has to be inlined) with one pinned `<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/...">` placed before the inline script that uses its global, instead of inlining the library's source or hand-writing a stand-in; the Artifact tool's description lists the few other script hosts the CSP admits. The page's own CSS and JS, its images and its data ship with the page. Most pages need no library at all - reach for one only when it carries real weight.

**Choose neutrals, don't default to them.** A pure mid-grey reads as unconsidered; a grey with a slight hue bias toward the page's accent reads as chosen. Pure white and near-black are fine grounds when they suit the subject - the point is that the neutral was picked, not inherited.

**Design both themes.** The page renders in the viewer's theme, and the viewer has three states, not two: an explicit choice stamps `data-theme="dark"` / `data-theme="light"` on the root element, and the default "system" setting stamps *nothing* - most viewers see the un-stamped document, where only `prefers-color-scheme` separates light from dark. Structure the CSS token-level for all three: the bare `:root` block defines the complete light palette (for a deliberately dark-first design, swap light and dark consistently through this whole pattern); `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` redefines only the tokens, guarded as `:root:not([data-theme="light"])` so an explicit light choice beats a dark OS; `:root[data-theme="dark"]` redefines them again so the toggle also wins in the other direction. Style components through the tokens, never directly inside a media or `[data-theme]` block - a color whose only definition sits behind `[data-theme]` never applies in the un-stamped state, and the page renders one theme's text on the other theme's ground. Two more rules keep each theme resolving as a set: the artifact composites over a ground the viewer paints in *its* theme, so `body` must set an explicit `background` from a token - a transparent body silently borrows the host's ground; and every element that sets a color takes it from the same token set as the surface behind it, never a literal that only works in one theme. Declare every token in the bare `:root` block before any media or `[data-theme]` block redefines it - a color that exists only inside one of those blocks is the classic unreadable-artifact bug. Give the second theme the same care as the first - don't naively invert; keep contrast legible and the accent working on both grounds. A design that deliberately commits to one visual world (a neon arcade screen, a letterpress invitation) may stay single-theme - then skip the media query and stamps entirely but still paint the background and every color explicitly, so the page holds on either host ground; make it a choice, not an omission.

**Let layout do the spacing.** Lay out sibling groups with flex or grid and `gap`, not per-element margins that silently collapse or double. Wide content - tables, code, diagrams - gets `overflow-x: auto` on its own container so the page body never scrolls sideways. Reach for `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` wherever digits line up in columns.

**Compose repeated things as one object.** Cards in a row, label/value pairs down a list, badges on siblings: same edges, baselines and inner padding from one to the next, and a recurring element sits in the same place on each. Let content set a container's height and pick a column count the items fill, so nothing stretches over dead space or sits alone in a row. Text that can outgrow its track wraps or scrolls in its own container; clipped text is a bug.

**Not everything is a card.** Border, fill, radius and shadow each say "separate object" - spend them by role, lifting the one thing that needs it, instead of one radius and one shadow stamped on every block, which flattens the hierarchy. Lead with big-number tiles only when those figures are the point of the page.

**Draw charts to the scale.** One scale places marks, ticks and labels, and every label names a value the chart reaches; chart text takes its color from the theme tokens so it reads in both themes; marks, labels and edges stay clear of one another and inside the drawing's bounds - in SVG, leave room in the viewBox for the outermost labels and give every drawn shape an explicit fill.

**Show the page at rest.** Everything meant to be read is visible once the page has loaded, without scrolling to trigger it - that first still frame is what a thumbnail, a shared link, and a skimming reader all get. A section may animate in, but from a visible resting state, never parked at `opacity: 0` waiting on an observer. Size a hero to what it holds, not to the viewport; a `100vh` opener pushes the page itself out of that first frame. A tool or app opens in a realistic working state - the user's real data where it exists, otherwise example rows, a loaded sample, a form someone plausibly filled, plainly marked as examples and never passed off as the user's own figures - so the first look shows what it does; an empty shell waiting for input shows nothing.

**Avoid AI-generated design** AI-generated design currently clusters around a few looks: warm cream (#F4F1EA) with a serif display and terracotta accent; near-black with a lone acid-green or vermilion pop; broadsheet hairline rules with dense columns; a purple-to-blue gradient hero on white; Inter or Space Grotesk as the "safe" face; emoji as section markers; everything centered; `rounded-lg` everywhere; accent bar/rail on rounded cards. Where the user pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly - their words always win, including when they ask for one of these looks. Where nothing is specified, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults.

**Build cleanly** Be cognizant of overlapping elements, cascade collisions, silent font fallbacks. Close every non-void element, double-quote attributes, give keyboard focus a visible state, respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. For generative or decorative graphics, reach for Canvas or WebGL rather than hand-authoring long SVG path data.

**CSS rules** When writing the CSS, watch your selector specificities. It is easy to generate classes that cancel each other out - a type-based selector like `.section` fighting an element-based one like `.cta` over padding and margins between sections. Structure the cascade so it doesn't silently undo your spacing.

**Writing the copy** Words are design material, not decoration. Write from the user's side of the screen - name things by what people recognize, not how the system is built (a person manages *notifications*, not *webhook config*). Active voice; a control says exactly what happens ("Publish", then a toast that says "Published"). Errors explain what went wrong and how to fix it - no apologies, no vagueness. Specific beats clever.

**Name the page like a product, not a caption.** The `<title>` is the artifact's name in the gallery and the browser tab, and it sets the reader's first impression of care. Give the page a real name: a short noun phrase, typically two to four words, specific to the subject - or, for a page that exists to answer one question, that question itself, which is then the page's name. Stop at the name - a title that carries its own explainer after a dash or colon reads as generated filler. The name must also identify the page among many: in the gallery it sits beside dozens of other artifacts, and a generic category label that could sit on any of them fails as a name just as surely as an appended explainer. When a candidate title pairs the name with a generic word - a greeting, a category, a page-type label - the name is the half to keep; a trim that drops the identity and keeps the generic word produces exactly the title that could sit on any page. And the rule removes explainers, it does not impose brevity: a multi-word title that already reads as one specific name is finished, and shortening it further only makes it generic. The one-sentence publish `description` is where the explanation belongs; the gallery shows it right under the title.

**Structure is information** Structural devices, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, should encode something true about the content, not decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence - like a real process or a typed timeline where order carries information the reader needs. Question if choices like numbered markers actually make sense before incorporating them.

**When it's a UI, not a document** A dashboard or tool is scanned and operated, not read top-to-bottom, so the craft shifts from typography to information design. Surface the summary before the detail; encode state in form as well as number - a pill, a chip, a severity stripe - so what needs attention reads at a glance. Semantic color (good / warning / critical) is separate from the accent hue and doesn't count as your accent. Give sparklines and charts the same care as type: an area fill, a faint grid, an emphasized endpoint. What's interactive should look interactive.



## Process

Before writing code, sketch a short design plan - a compact token system with color, type, and layout:
- **Color**: describe the palette as 4-6 named hex values.
- **Type**: typefaces for 2+ roles - a characterful display face used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed.
- **Layout**: a layout concept in one or two sentences.

Then build, following the plan and deriving every color and type decision from it.

**Write, look once, publish.** Before publishing you may look at the rendered page once - one screenshot of the local file, or the Artifact tool's preview where it offers one - then one pass of edits for what it shows, without a second look. For a page that charts real numbers, take that look rather than skip it, and spend it on the chart. Don't build a test loop around your own file: no repeated screenshots, no pulling the script out to run it through node, no scripts that probe the DOM. That loop spends the session re-checking what a careful write already settled, while the user waits for a link. Then publish, check once any `window.claude` call the preview couldn't run, and stop: the live page is the review surface, and further polish is the user's to ask for. If the user reports something visibly broken - a clipped column, unreadable text, a control that does nothing - fix that and republish once.

## When the request is editorial

The stance shifts: the client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view. Make opinionated calls, and take one real aesthetic risk where it serves the work.

Review the design plan against the subject before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page, revise that part, and note what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the plan's uniqueness do you write the code, following the revised plan exactly.

**Principles** 

- The hero is a thesis: open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world - headline, image, live demo, interactive moment. 
- Typography carries the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, not the same families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content. 
- Leverage motion deliberately. Think about where and if animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. An orchestrated moment usually lands harder than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation contributes to the feeling that the design is AI-generated. 
- Match complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.
- Spend your boldness in one place; keep everything around it quiet. If the accent fights the ground, shift it toward analogous or drop saturation rather than replacing it.

name: Durable release

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: durable-release-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  verify:
    name: Verify release candidate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Build local Callisto
        uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local

      - name: Install just
        uses: extractions/setup-just@53165ef7e734c5c07cb06b3c8e7b647c5aa16db3 # v4.0.0
        with:
          just-version: '1.58.0'

      - name: Format Check
        run: just fmt-check

      - name: Clippy Lints
        run: just lint

      - name: Install release verification tools
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@0758d235715de2f3551eacc980d9ae8fce9342c3 # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-nextest,ripgrep

      - name: Unit & Integration Tests
        run: just test

      - name: WASM Target Check
        run: just wasm-check

      - name: Install cargo-deny
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@0758d235715de2f3551eacc980d9ae8fce9342c3 # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-deny

      - name: Supply Chain Audit
        run: just audit

      - name: Reject mutable GitHub Actions references
        run: .github/tests/verify-action-pins.sh

  version-pr:
    name: Create or update the Callisto release PR
    needs: verify
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
    outputs:
      has_pending_changesets: ${{ steps.version-pr.outputs.hasChangesets }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - name: Compose, version, and open the release PR
        id: version-pr
        uses: $/.github/actions/callisto-action
        with:
          setup_callisto: 'false'
          branch: main
          release_branch: callisto/version-packages
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

  release-candidate:
    name: Identify a merged Callisto release PR
    needs: [verify, version-pr]
    if: needs.version-pr.outputs.has_pending_changesets == 'false'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      is_release_pr: ${{ steps.candidate.outputs.is_release_pr }}
    steps:
      - id: candidate
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # This only schedules the job. `release plan` verifies the actual
          # parent-to-merge delta; labels and PR metadata are never authority.
          # The GitHub API check is complementary provenance evidence: a
          # trusted merge must be both an actual merge of the managed PR and
          # a GitHub-verified signed commit. It cannot be a direct push.
          prs=$(gh api --paginate "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${GITHUB_SHA}/pulls" --jq '[.[] | select(.merged_at != null and .base.ref == "main" and (.head.ref == "callisto/version-packages" or (.head.ref | test("^callisto/version-packages--[0-9a-f]{40}$"))))] | length')
          verified=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${GITHUB_SHA}" --jq '.commit.verification.verified')
          if [[ "$prs" == 1 && "$verified" == true ]]; then
            echo 'is_release_pr=true' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo 'is_release_pr=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  plan:
    name: Derive ephemeral intent from the merged release commit
    needs: release-candidate
    if: needs.release-candidate.outputs.is_release_pr == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - name: Derive and hash intent
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          callisto release plan --from-release-commit "$GITHUB_SHA" --out release-intent.json
          shasum -a 256 release-intent.json > release-intent.json.sha256
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: |
            release-intent.json
            release-intent.json.sha256
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 1

  build:
    name: Build the intent-bound source tree
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      attestations: write
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: extractions/setup-just@53165ef7e734c5c07cb06b3c8e7b647c5aa16db3 # v4.0.0
        with:
          just-version: '1.58.0'
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: .release-handoff
      - name: Verify handoff and build
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          (cd .release-handoff && shasum -a 256 -c release-intent.json.sha256)
          callisto release inspect --input .release-handoff/release-intent.json
          mkdir -p release-artifacts
          just build
      - name: Attest declared binary artifacts
        if: hashFiles('release-artifacts/**') != ''
        uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@4d101475d8b20a2381f78447822ac1eab6504dd8 # v4.2.2
        with:
          subject-path: release-artifacts/**
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: release-build
          path: |
            .release-handoff
            release-artifacts
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 1

  environment-policy:
    name: Verify release Environment protection
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      actions: read
    steps:
      - name: Require release Environment reviewers
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          reviewers=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/environments/release" --jq '.protection_rules // [] | map(select(.type == "required_reviewers")) | length')
          [[ "$reviewers" != 0 ]] || { echo '::error::GitHub Environment release has no required-reviewers protection rule'; exit 1; }

  execute:
    name: Execute approved release
    needs: environment-policy
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: release
    permissions:
      contents: write
      attestations: read
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: .release-intent
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-build
          path: .release-build
      - name: Verify same-run handoff before credentials
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          (cd .release-intent && shasum -a 256 -c release-intent.json.sha256)
          cmp .release-intent/release-intent.json .release-build/release-intent.json
      - name: Execute verified release
        env:
          CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
          NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
          TWINE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.TWINE_PASSWORD }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          state_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-release-state/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
          mkdir -p "$state_dir"
          args=(--intent .release-intent/release-intent.json --state "$state_dir/execution-state.json")
          if [[ -f .release-build/release-artifacts/manifest.json ]]; then
            args+=(--artifact-manifest .release-build/release-artifacts/manifest.json --artifact-dir .release-build/release-artifacts)
          fi
          callisto release execute "${args[@]}"

name: Release

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: durable-release-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  verify:
    name: Verify release candidate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Build local Callisto
        uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local

      - name: Install just
        uses: extractions/setup-just@53165ef7e734c5c07cb06b3c8e7b647c5aa16db3 # v4.0.0
        with:
          just-version: '1.58.0'

      - name: Format Check
        run: just fmt-check

      - name: Clippy Lints
        run: just lint

      - name: Install release verification tools
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@0758d235715de2f3551eacc980d9ae8fce9342c3 # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-nextest,ripgrep

      - name: Unit & Integration Tests
        run: just test

      - name: WASM Target Check
        run: just wasm-check

      - name: Install cargo-deny
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@0758d235715de2f3551eacc980d9ae8fce9342c3 # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-deny

      - name: Supply Chain Audit
        run: just audit

      - name: Reject mutable GitHub Actions references
        run: .github/tests/verify-action-pins.sh

  version-pr:
    name: Create or update the Callisto release PR
    needs: verify
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
    outputs:
      has_pending_changesets: ${{ steps.version-pr.outputs.hasChangesets }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - name: Compose, version, and open the release PR
        id: version-pr
        uses: $/.github/actions/callisto-action
        with:
          setup_callisto: 'false'
          branch: main
          release_branch: callisto/version-packages
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

  release-candidate:
    name: Identify a merged Callisto release PR
    needs: [verify, version-pr]
    if: needs.version-pr.outputs.has_pending_changesets == 'false'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      is_release_pr: ${{ steps.candidate.outputs.is_release_pr }}
    steps:
      - id: candidate
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # This only schedules the job. `release plan` verifies the actual
          # parent-to-merge delta; labels and PR metadata are never authority.
          # The GitHub API check is complementary provenance evidence: a
          # trusted merge must be both an actual merge of the managed PR and
          # a GitHub-verified signed commit. It cannot be a direct push.
          prs=$(gh api --paginate "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${GITHUB_SHA}/pulls" --jq '[.[] | select(.merged_at != null and .base.ref == "main" and (.head.ref == "callisto/version-packages" or (.head.ref | test("^callisto/version-packages--[0-9a-f]{40}$"))))] | length')
          verified=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${GITHUB_SHA}" --jq '.commit.verification.verified')
          if [[ "$prs" == 1 && "$verified" == true ]]; then
            echo 'is_release_pr=true' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo 'is_release_pr=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  plan:
    name: Derive ephemeral intent from the merged release commit
    needs: release-candidate
    if: needs.release-candidate.outputs.is_release_pr == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - name: Derive and hash intent
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          callisto release plan --from-release-commit "$GITHUB_SHA" --out release-intent.json
          shasum -a 256 release-intent.json > release-intent.json.sha256
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: |
            release-intent.json
            release-intent.json.sha256
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 1

  build:
    name: Build the intent-bound source tree
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      attestations: write
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: extractions/setup-just@53165ef7e734c5c07cb06b3c8e7b647c5aa16db3 # v4.0.0
        with:
          just-version: '1.58.0'
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: .release-handoff
      - name: Verify handoff and build
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          (cd .release-handoff && shasum -a 256 -c release-intent.json.sha256)
          callisto release inspect --input .release-handoff/release-intent.json
          mkdir -p release-artifacts
          just build
      - name: Attest declared binary artifacts
        if: hashFiles('release-artifacts/**') != ''
        uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@4d101475d8b20a2381f78447822ac1eab6504dd8 # v4.2.2
        with:
          subject-path: release-artifacts/**
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: release-build
          path: |
            .release-handoff
            release-artifacts
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 1

  environment-policy:
    name: Verify release Environment protection
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      actions: read
    steps:
      - name: Require release Environment reviewers
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          reviewers=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/environments/release" --jq '.protection_rules // [] | map(select(.type == "required_reviewers")) | length')
          [[ "$reviewers" != 0 ]] || { echo '::error::GitHub Environment release has no required-reviewers protection rule'; exit 1; }

  execute:
    name: Execute approved release
    needs: environment-policy
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: release
    permissions:
      contents: write
      attestations: read
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: .release-intent
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-build
          path: .release-build
      - name: Verify same-run handoff before credentials
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          (cd .release-intent && shasum -a 256 -c release-intent.json.sha256)
          cmp .release-intent/release-intent.json .release-build/release-intent.json
      - name: Execute verified release
        env:
          CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
          NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
          TWINE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.TWINE_PASSWORD }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          state_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-release-state/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
          mkdir -p "$state_dir"
          args=(--intent .release-intent/release-intent.json --state "$state_dir/execution-state.json")
          if [[ -f .release-build/release-artifacts/manifest.json ]]; then
            args+=(--artifact-manifest .release-build/release-artifacts/manifest.json --artifact-dir .release-build/release-artifacts)
          fi
          callisto release execute "${args[@]}"

Yes, I think full ID migration is the right call — and now that I've mapped it precisely, it's a clean, bounded change:

**In scope** (5 files, ~35 reference sites): rename `SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001A/B/C` → new IDs (renaming the files + their own `id` fields + their 22 references to each other), then fix up the 7 references in `SPEC-GITHUB-RELEASE-HARDENING-003.json` and 4 in `SPEC-RELEASE-SOURCE-PROVENANCE-002.json`.

I'd also reword the leftover "durable"/"durability" prose inside those three files to match, in the same pass.

Go ahead with `PERSISTENCE`, or did you have a different word in mind?

content.text:
This is a real, pre-existing bug — not something I introduced or missed in recent work. It's in code that predates everything from this session, and it's never been caught because **no release has ever gotten this far in the pipeline before today** (we already proved `execute` has literally never run in this repo's history — now we know why: `plan`, the step right before it, was silently broken too).

**Root cause:** `derive_release_commit_decision()` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_decision.rs:109`) re-derives the release decision by diffing the merged commit against its parent, and only recognizes a package's version bump as "authorized" if a changeset **directly names that exact package**. I checked all 11 consumed changesets — only `callisto-model`, `callisto-graph`, `callisto-cli`, and `callisto-vcs` are ever named:

```
filter-plan-by-report:    callisto-model, callisto-graph, callisto-cli
jolly-ravens-strut:       callisto-model, callisto-cli
release-pr-forge-commit-api: callisto-model
release-pr-commit-plan-cli:  callisto-cli
release-pr-staged-changes-vcs: callisto-vcs
... (rest are graph/cli only)
```

But `callisto.toml` defines a `[[fixed-group]] name = "workspace"` covering **7 packages** (including `callisto-changelog`, `callisto-conventional`, `callisto-fixtures`, `callisto-format`, `callisto-manifests`, `callisto-moon`) that must always version together — so those bump from 0.5.0→0.6.0 too, purely via cascade, with no changeset ever naming them directly. The validator sees their version changed with nothing in its `selected` set explaining it, and fails closed exactly as designed: *"A changed version without a consumed changeset is an unreviewed extra release."*

The check is doing its job correctly — it's just missing a whole category of legitimate cause. It knows nothing about fixed-group cascades, linked groups, dependency-driven cascades, or pre-release policy (the four `ReleaseInclusionReason` variants that `plan_version` already models when it *creates* the bump — this function just never learned to recognize them when re-deriving it from a commit afterward).

This needs a real fix in `derive_release_commit_decision`, teaching it to accept a version change when it's explained by cascade membership, not just a direct changeset. Given `callisto`'s own release will never pass `plan` without this fix, and it's genuinely a correctness gap (not a config issue on your end), want me to scope and fix this properly?

Wire three already-implemented but currently disconnected/broken pieces of callisto's fixed-group version engine into the real command call paths: (1) make fixed-group siblings converge on a single shared group-aligned target version instead of each bumping independently from its own base, by adding a new Fixed-group convergence block to cascade.rs's solve_cascade — structurally mirroring the pre-existing Linked-group convergence block at lines 314-379 — that iterates input.groups.fixed.values(), computes one shared target via the existing fixed_group_target function, and assigns that target to every member of each Fixed group, participating in the same `while changed` fixpoint loop; (2) call the existing, fully-implemented pre_mutation_checks divergence/napi-drift detector from callisto-graph's real version-command orchestration path, before mutation, and actually consume its result (merge diagnostics, abort on divergence error); (3) add cross-group conflict detection to GroupTable::resolve so that two differently-spelled group members that resolve to the same PackageId across two different groups produce GraphError::ConflictingGroupMembership instead of silently overwriting one group's claim with the other's.

converged target the instant any member bumps (Track 1) -- so any real
release touching a group failed closed with E124 "release intent no
longer matches the current workspace snapshot", even though the bump

content.text:
PR opened: **https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/pull/53**

Summary of what was found and fixed:

**Root cause**: `derive_release_commit_decision` (the function `release plan --from-release-commit` uses to re-verify a merged release PR) only ever recognized a package's version bump as authorized when a changeset named it *directly*. It had no concept of fixed/linked-group cascades — and `callisto`'s own `workspace` fixed group covers 7 of its 10 crates, none of which ever get named directly by a changeset. Every release has been failing here since the first correctly-signed merge, which is exactly why `execute` has never run once in this repo's history.

**The fix**: expand the authorized-package set using the workspace's existing `fixed_of`/`linked_of` group lookups, without re-implementing or re-running the full dependency-cascade solver — group convergence guarantees every member lands on the *same* target version, which is cheaply and independently verifiable straight from the commit diff. Added a new `E155` error that fails closed if a group's members ever *don't* converge (catches a tampered commit rather than silently trusting it).

**Bonus find**: writing the test for this surfaced a second live instance of the exact `rename_all`-doesn't-rename-variant-fields bug from earlier this session — `ReleaseInclusionReason` was serializing `group_id` as snake_case. Fixed in the same PR.

**Verified for real, not just in tests**: rebuilt the binary and replayed it directly against the actual commit that failed in production (`7444599d`, the run you originally flagged) — it now produces a correct decision.

Two unrelated things noticed along the way, not touched here:
1. `Cargo.lock` on `main` is out of sync with the manifest versions (still shows `0.5.0` after PR #51 bumped everything to `0.6.0`) — separate, minor drift.
2. Two throwaway spike repos from earlier still need deleting (`orin-dx/callisto-relpr-spike`, `-spike-public`) — I still lack `delete_repo` scope.

content.text:
Verified directly from source rather than memory: `changesets/action`'s publish step runs the actual `changeset publish` CLI, which iterates workspace packages and asks the registry "is this version already published?" — publishing whatever isn't. That's it. No git diff, no changeset-provenance check, no re-derivation of anything.

## How knope/changesets actually do this

**changesets**: Version-PR creation (what we researched earlier) computes bumps from changesets + linked-package config. Once merged, `changeset publish` looks only at the *current* `package.json` versions on disk versus what's on npm right now, and publishes the delta. It has zero awareness of git history, PRs, or changesets by the time publish runs — the registry itself is the only "already done" check.

**knope**: Same shape. It computes a release from conventional-commit/changelog state and publishes based on current versions, not by cryptographically re-verifying that a merged commit's diff traces back to specific authorized changesets.

Neither tool asks "does every version bump in this commit trace to something a human actually reviewed" — they trust whatever's in the working tree at merge time, full stop.

## Is Callisto's extra check necessary?

Two different questions bundled in "necessary," and they have different answers:

**Is *some* provenance check on the release-PR merge worth having?** Yes — and that part isn't in question here. Requiring a GitHub-verified signed merge of a PR whose branch matches the managed pattern (what we spent the last several days fixing) is a real, meaningful trust boundary neither changesets nor knope bother with at all. That stays.

**Is re-deriving the *entire per-package decision* from raw git diff, independently reimplementing cascade-expansion logic, actually buying something worth its cost?** This is the part worth questioning. It found a real bug just now — but notice *why*: it's a second, independent implementation of "how does a fixed-group cascade expand," built separately from the one in `cascade.rs`/`plan_version` that computed the *original*, correct decision. Two implementations of the same logic is exactly the kind of thing that drifts and breaks, which is precisely what happened. The fix I shipped teaches the second implementation about two of four cascade shapes; `Cascade` and `PreReleasePolicy` are still gaps by construction, and any future third cascade behavior will need this same treatment a third time.

## What we're actually trying to accomplish

Strip away the mechanism and the real goal is: **prove that what's about to be published is exactly what a human reviewed in the release PR — no more, no less.** That's a legitimate, valuable goal (it would catch a Callisto bug that made an extra unintended bump, not just a malicious actor). But the current mechanism achieves it the hard way: reconstruct the decision from scratch via git plumbing, using a second, parallel implementation of cascade logic that has to independently agree with the first one forever.

There's a comment already sitting in `release.rs` that says the quiet part out loud — `ReleaseInclusionReason` is deliberately "a model value... so every later process can validate the exact approved roster without importing graph." That's describing a **persist-and-verify** design, not a **recompute-and-hope-it-matches** one. The current `derive_release_commit_decision` never actually does what that comment describes.

## Proposed plan

Have the release-PR generation step **persist the real `ReleaseDecisionV1`** it already computed correctly (full `FixedGroup`/`LinkedGroup`/`Cascade`/`PreReleasePolicy` reasoning, computed once, in the one place that already knows how) as part of the commit — e.g. a `.changeset/.release-decision.json` sidecar written alongside the manifest/changelog edits. Then replace `derive_release_commit_decision`'s job with something much simpler: **read that file back and verify it matches the diff exactly** — every claimed entry's manifest+changelog actually changed to the claimed version, and nothing else changed. No cascade-expansion reimplementation at all; cascade logic exists in exactly one place, forever.

This is:
- **Simpler** — verification becomes a straightforward equality check instead of a parallel policy engine.
- **More correct** — automatically covers `Cascade`/`PreReleasePolicy` too, since it's trusting the *real* computation instead of a partial re-implementation of it.
- **Still strictly more rigorous than changesets/knope** — it still requires a signed, pattern-matched, human-reviewed merge, and still fails closed if the diff doesn't match what was claimed.
- **A real, separate change** — not a small patch. It touches the release-PR generation path (add the sidecar write), the commit-plan/forge-API executor (carry the file through, keep it out of the forbidden-paths list), and replaces `derive_release_commit_decision`'s body, plus its own spec.

I'd scope it as its own spec/plan rather than bolt it onto anything in flight. Want me to draft that spec, or talk through the design more first?

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Executes a typed Callisto release-PR decision. Forge reads stay here; all
3	# create/update policy belongs to `callisto release-pr decide`.
4	#
5	# The managed branch is never pushed with the Git wire protocol: on a public
6	# repository, GITHUB_TOKEN cannot write `.github/workflows/*` that way, nor
7	# through createCommitOnBranch's own fileChanges, on any ref (confirmed
8	# directly against this repository). Instead, the generated
9	# version-bump changes are committed via the forge commit API onto a
10	# deterministic staging branch rooted at the current base commit -- which
11	# never needs to touch `.github/workflows/*`, since that path is inherited
12	# unchanged from the base -- and only then is the managed branch's ref moved
13	# onto that commit. A ref move is not itself a write to that path.
14	set -euo pipefail
15	
16	cd "$INPUT_CWD"
17	
18	# This checkout starts on the configured base. Preserve its exact commit for
19	# both observations; the working tree changes below (git add -A) never
20	# create a local commit -- the real commit is made remotely, via the forge
21	# commit API, on the staging branch.
22	base_commit=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
23	
24	release_pr_snapshot() {
25	  local raw_prs
26	  raw_prs=$(gh pr list --state open --base "$INPUT_BRANCH" --limit 1000 --json number,headRefName,headRepository,headRefOid)
27	  jq -cn \
28	    --arg repository "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
29	    --arg base_branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" \
30	    --arg base_commit "$base_commit" \
31	    --argjson raw_prs "$raw_prs" \
32	    '{
33	      schemaVersion: 2,
34	      repository: $repository,
35	      baseBranch: $base_branch,
36	      baseCommit: $base_commit,
37	      openPullRequests: [$raw_prs[] | {
38	        number,
39	        headRepository: (.headRepository.nameWithOwner // ""),
40	        headBranch: .headRefName,
41	        headCommit: .headRefOid
42	      }]
43	    }'
44	}
45	
46	snapshot=$(release_pr_snapshot)
47	decision=$(callisto --format json release-pr decide \
48	  --snapshot "$snapshot" \
49	  --repository "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
50	  --base-branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" \
51	  --release-branch "$INPUT_RELEASE_BRANCH")
52	decision_kind=$(jq -r '.action.kind' <<< "$decision")
53	
54	case "$decision_kind" in
55	  noop)
56	    echo 'hasChangesets=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
57	    matrix=$(callisto matrix --format json | jq -c '[.platformTargets[].targets[]] | unique_by(.artifactName)')
58	    echo "nativeMatrix=$matrix" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
59	    echo '::notice::No changesets. This action does not publish, tag, download artifacts, or create releases; use the durable repository workflow.'
60	    exit 0
61	    ;;
62	  create)
63	    release_branch=$(jq -r '.action.branch' <<< "$decision")
64	    staging_branch=$(jq -r '.action.stagingBranch' <<< "$decision")
65	    existing_pr=''
66	    ;;
67	  update)
68	    existing_pr=$(jq -r '.action.pullRequestNumber' <<< "$decision")
69	    release_branch=$(jq -r '.action.branch' <<< "$decision")
70	    staging_branch=$(jq -r '.action.stagingBranch' <<< "$decision")
71	    ;;
72	  *) echo "::error::Callisto returned unsupported release PR decision kind: $decision_kind"; exit 1 ;;
73	esac
74	
75	echo 'hasChangesets=true' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
76	if [[ -n "$existing_pr" ]]; then
77	  existing_body=$(gh pr view "$existing_pr" --json body --jq '.body')
78	  body=$(printf '%s' "$existing_body" | callisto compose-pr-body --existing-body - --label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" --branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" --format text)
79	else
80	  body=$(callisto compose-pr-body --label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" --branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" --format text)
81	fi
82	
83	read -ra command <<< "$INPUT_VERSION_COMMAND"
84	"${command[@]}"
85	git add -A
86	test -n "$(git status --porcelain)" || { echo '::error::pending changesets produced no release-PR delta'; exit 1; }
87	
88	plan_file=$(mktemp)
89	callisto --format json release-pr commit-plan --base-commit "$base_commit" --message "$INPUT_COMMIT_MESSAGE" --out "$plan_file"
90	local_tree=$(git write-tree)
91	
92	staging_created=false
93	cleanup_staging() {
94	  if [[ "$staging_created" == true ]]; then
95	    gh api -X DELETE "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs/heads/$staging_branch" > /dev/null 2>&1 \
96	      || echo "::warning::could not delete staging branch $staging_branch; the next run reclaims this deterministic name"
97	  fi
98	  rm -f "$plan_file" body.json
99	}
100	trap cleanup_staging EXIT
101	
102	# A local diff does not authorize a stale forge write. Re-observe immediately
103	# before mutating the remote branch, then again before moving the managed
104	# ref, then again before GitHub label/PR writes.
105	callisto release-pr verify --decision "$decision" --snapshot "$(release_pr_snapshot)" > /dev/null
106	
107	if gh api -X PATCH "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs/heads/$staging_branch" -f sha="$base_commit" -F force=true > /dev/null 2>&1; then
108	  :
109	else
110	  gh api -X POST "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs" -f ref="refs/heads/$staging_branch" -f sha="$base_commit" > /dev/null
111	fi
112	staging_created=true
113	
114	jq -n \
115	  --arg repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
116	  --arg branch "$staging_branch" \
117	  --arg headline "$INPUT_COMMIT_MESSAGE" \
118	  --slurpfile plan "$plan_file" \
119	  '{
120	    query: "mutation($input: CreateCommitOnBranchInput!) { createCommitOnBranch(input: $input) { commit { oid } } }",
121	    variables: {
122	      input: {
123	        branch: {repositoryNameWithOwner: $repo, branchName: $branch},
124	        message: {headline: $headline},
125	        expectedHeadOid: $plan[0].baseCommit,
126	        fileChanges: {
127	          additions: [$plan[0].additions[] | {path, contents: .contentsBase64}],
128	          deletions: $plan[0].deletions
129	        }
130	      }
131	    }
132	  }' > body.json
133	
134	new_sha=$(gh api graphql --input body.json --jq '.data.createCommitOnBranch.commit.oid')
135	remote_tree=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/commits/$new_sha" --jq '.tree.sha')
136	if [[ "$remote_tree" != "$local_tree" ]]; then
137	  echo "::error::forge commit tree $remote_tree does not match the locally staged tree $local_tree; refusing to move $release_branch"

139	fi

141	callisto release-pr verify --decision "$decision" --snapshot "$(release_pr_snapshot)" > /dev/null
142

144	  gh api -X PATCH "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs/heads/$release_branch" -f sha="$new_sha" -F force=true > /dev/null

file.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Executes a typed Callisto release-PR decision. Forge reads stay here; all
# create/update policy belongs to `callisto release-pr decide`.
#
# The managed branch is never pushed with the Git wire protocol: on a public
# repository, GITHUB_TOKEN cannot write `.github/workflows/*` that way, nor
# through createCommitOnBranch's own fileChanges, on any ref (confirmed
# directly against this repository). Instead, the generated
# version-bump changes are committed via the forge commit API onto a
# deterministic staging branch rooted at the current base commit -- which
# never needs to touch `.github/workflows/*`, since that path is inherited
# unchanged from the base -- and only then is the managed branch's ref moved
# onto that commit. A ref move is not itself a write to that path.
set -euo pipefail

cd "$INPUT_CWD"

# This checkout starts on the configured base. Preserve its exact commit for
# both observations; the working tree changes below (git add -A) never
# create a local commit -- the real commit is made remotely, via the forge
# commit API, on the staging branch.
base_commit=$(git rev-parse HEAD)

release_pr_snapshot() {
  local raw_prs
  raw_prs=$(gh pr list --state open --base "$INPUT_BRANCH" --limit 1000 --json number,headRefName,headRepository,headRefOid)
  jq -cn \
    --arg repository "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
    --arg base_branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" \
    --arg base_commit "$base_commit" \
    --argjson raw_prs "$raw_prs" \
    '{
      schemaVersion: 2,
      repository: $repository,
      baseBranch: $base_branch,
      baseCommit: $base_commit,
      openPullRequests: [$raw_prs[] | {
        number,
        headRepository: (.headRepository.nameWithOwner // ""),
        headBranch: .headRefName,
        headCommit: .headRefOid
      }]
    }'
}

snapshot=$(release_pr_snapshot)
decision=$(callisto --format json release-pr decide \
  --snapshot "$snapshot" \
  --repository "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
  --base-branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" \
  --release-branch "$INPUT_RELEASE_BRANCH")
decision_kind=$(jq -r '.action.kind' <<< "$decision")

case "$decision_kind" in
  noop)
    echo 'hasChangesets=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    matrix=$(callisto matrix --format json | jq -c '[.platformTargets[].targets[]] | unique_by(.artifactName)')
    echo "nativeMatrix=$matrix" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo '::notice::No changesets. This action does not publish, tag, download artifacts, or create releases; use the durable repository workflow.'
    exit 0
    ;;
  create)
    release_branch=$(jq -r '.action.branch' <<< "$decision")
    staging_branch=$(jq -r '.action.stagingBranch' <<< "$decision")
    existing_pr=''
    ;;
  update)
    existing_pr=$(jq -r '.action.pullRequestNumber' <<< "$decision")
    release_branch=$(jq -r '.action.branch' <<< "$decision")
    staging_branch=$(jq -r '.action.stagingBranch' <<< "$decision")
    ;;
  *) echo "::error::Callisto returned unsupported release PR decision kind: $decision_kind"; exit 1 ;;
esac

echo 'hasChangesets=true' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
if [[ -n "$existing_pr" ]]; then
  existing_body=$(gh pr view "$existing_pr" --json body --jq '.body')
  body=$(printf '%s' "$existing_body" | callisto compose-pr-body --existing-body - --label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" --branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" --format text)
else
  body=$(callisto compose-pr-body --label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" --branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" --format text)
fi

read -ra command <<< "$INPUT_VERSION_COMMAND"
"${command[@]}"
git add -A
test -n "$(git status --porcelain)" || { echo '::error::pending changesets produced no release-PR delta'; exit 1; }

plan_file=$(mktemp)
callisto --format json release-pr commit-plan --base-commit "$base_commit" --message "$INPUT_COMMIT_MESSAGE" --out "$plan_file"
local_tree=$(git write-tree)

staging_created=false
cleanup_staging() {
  if [[ "$staging_created" == true ]]; then
    gh api -X DELETE "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs/heads/$staging_branch" > /dev/null 2>&1 \
      || echo "::warning::could not delete staging branch $staging_branch; the next run reclaims this deterministic name"
  fi
  rm -f "$plan_file" body.json
}
trap cleanup_staging EXIT

# A local diff does not authorize a stale forge write. Re-observe immediately
# before mutating the remote branch, then again before moving the managed
# ref, then again before GitHub label/PR writes.
callisto release-pr verify --decision "$decision" --snapshot "$(release_pr_snapshot)" > /dev/null

if gh api -X PATCH "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs/heads/$staging_branch" -f sha="$base_commit" -F force=true > /dev/null 2>&1; then
  :
else
  gh api -X POST "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs" -f ref="refs/heads/$staging_branch" -f sha="$base_commit" > /dev/null
fi
staging_created=true

jq -n \
  --arg repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
  --arg branch "$staging_branch" \
  --arg headline "$INPUT_COMMIT_MESSAGE" \
  --slurpfile plan "$plan_file" \
  '{
    query: "mutation($input: CreateCommitOnBranchInput!) { createCommitOnBranch(input: $input) { commit { oid } } }",
    variables: {
      input: {
        branch: {repositoryNameWithOwner: $repo, branchName: $branch},
        message: {headline: $headline},
        expectedHeadOid: $plan[0].baseCommit,
        fileChanges: {
          additions: [$plan[0].additions[] | {path, contents: .contentsBase64}],
          deletions: $plan[0].deletions
        }
      }
    }
  }' > body.json

new_sha=$(gh api graphql --input body.json --jq '.data.createCommitOnBranch.commit.oid')
remote_tree=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/commits/$new_sha" --jq '.tree.sha')
if [[ "$remote_tree" != "$local_tree" ]]; then
  echo "::error::forge commit tree $remote_tree does not match the locally staged tree $local_tree; refusing to move $release_branch"
  exit 1
fi

callisto release-pr verify --decision "$decision" --snapshot "$(release_pr_snapshot)" > /dev/null

if [[ "$decision_kind" == update ]]; then
  gh api -X PATCH "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs/heads/$release_branch" -f sha="$new_sha" -F force=true > /dev/null
else
  if ! gh api -X POST "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs" -f ref="refs/heads/$release_branch" -f sha="$new_sha" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
    gh api -X PATCH "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs/heads/$release_branch" -f sha="$new_sha" -F force=true > /dev/null
  fi
fi
moved_sha=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs/heads/$release_branch" --jq '.object.sha')
if [[ "$moved_sha" != "$new_sha" ]]; then
  echo "::error::$release_branch points at $moved_sha after the update, expected $new_sha; a concurrent write may have raced this run"
  exit 1
fi

callisto release-pr verify --decision "$decision" --snapshot "$(release_pr_snapshot)" > /dev/null

label_exists=$(gh label list --limit 1000 --json name --jq 'any(.[]; .name == env.INPUT_PR_LABEL)')
if [[ "$label_exists" != true ]]; then
  gh label create "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" --color 0e8a16 --description 'Callisto release packages'
fi

case "$decision_kind" in
  create)
    gh pr create --head "$release_branch" --base "$INPUT_BRANCH" --title "$INPUT_TITLE" --body "$body" --label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL"
    ;;
  update)
    gh pr edit "$existing_pr" --title "$INPUT_TITLE" --body "$body" --add-label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL"
    ;;
esac

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Executes a typed Callisto release-PR decision. Forge reads stay here; all
# create/update policy belongs to `callisto release-pr decide`.
#
# The managed branch is never pushed with the Git wire protocol: on a public
# repository, GITHUB_TOKEN cannot write `.github/workflows/*` that way, nor
# through createCommitOnBranch's own fileChanges, on any ref (confirmed
# directly against this repository). Instead, the generated
# version-bump changes are committed via the forge commit API onto a
# deterministic staging branch rooted at the current base commit -- which
# never needs to touch `.github/workflows/*`, since that path is inherited
# unchanged from the base -- and only then is the managed branch's ref moved
# onto that commit. A ref move is not itself a write to that path.
set -euo pipefail

cd "$INPUT_CWD"

# This checkout starts on the configured base. Preserve its exact commit for
# both observations; the working tree changes below (git add -A) never
# create a local commit -- the real commit is made remotely, via the forge
# commit API, on the staging branch.
base_commit=$(git rev-parse HEAD)

release_pr_snapshot() {
  local raw_prs
  raw_prs=$(gh pr list --state open --base "$INPUT_BRANCH" --limit 1000 --json number,headRefName,headRepository,headRefOid)
  jq -cn \
    --arg repository "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
    --arg base_branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" \
    --arg base_commit "$base_commit" \
    --argjson raw_prs "$raw_prs" \
    '{
      schemaVersion: 2,
      repository: $repository,
      baseBranch: $base_branch,
      baseCommit: $base_commit,
      openPullRequests: [$raw_prs[] | {
        number,
        headRepository: (.headRepository.nameWithOwner // ""),
        headBranch: .headRefName,
        headCommit: .headRefOid
      }]
    }'
}

snapshot=$(release_pr_snapshot)
decision=$(callisto --format json release-pr decide \
  --snapshot "$snapshot" \
  --repository "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
  --base-branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" \
  --release-branch "$INPUT_RELEASE_BRANCH")
decision_kind=$(jq -r '.action.kind' <<< "$decision")

case "$decision_kind" in
  noop)
    echo 'hasChangesets=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    matrix=$(callisto matrix --format json | jq -c '[.platformTargets[].targets[]] | unique_by(.artifactName)')
    echo "nativeMatrix=$matrix" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo '::notice::No changesets. This action does not publish, tag, download artifacts, or create releases; use the durable repository workflow.'
    exit 0
    ;;
  create)
    release_branch=$(jq -r '.action.branch' <<< "$decision")
    staging_branch=$(jq -r '.action.stagingBranch' <<< "$decision")
    existing_pr=''
    ;;
  update)
    existing_pr=$(jq -r '.action.pullRequestNumber' <<< "$decision")
    release_branch=$(jq -r '.action.branch' <<< "$decision")
    staging_branch=$(jq -r '.action.stagingBranch' <<< "$decision")
    ;;
  *) echo "::error::Callisto returned unsupported release PR decision kind: $decision_kind"; exit 1 ;;
esac

echo 'hasChangesets=true' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
if [[ -n "$existing_pr" ]]; then
  existing_body=$(gh pr view "$existing_pr" --json body --jq '.body')
  body=$(printf '%s' "$existing_body" | callisto compose-pr-body --existing-body - --label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" --branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" --format text)
else
  body=$(callisto compose-pr-body --label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" --branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" --format text)
fi

read -ra command <<< "$INPUT_VERSION_COMMAND"
"${command[@]}"
git add -A
test -n "$(git status --porcelain)" || { echo '::error::pending changesets produced no release-PR delta'; exit 1; }

plan_file=$(mktemp)
callisto --format json release-pr commit-plan --base-commit "$base_commit" --message "$INPUT_COMMIT_MESSAGE" --out "$plan_file"
local_tree=$(git write-tree)

staging_created=false
cleanup_staging() {
  if [[ "$staging_created" == true ]]; then
    gh api -X DELETE "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs/heads/$staging_branch" > /dev/null 2>&1 \
      || echo "::warning::could not delete staging branch $staging_branch; the next run reclaims this deterministic name"
  fi
  rm -f "$plan_file" body.json
}
trap cleanup_staging EXIT

# A local diff does not authorize a stale forge write. Re-observe immediately
# before mutating the remote branch, then again before moving the managed
# ref, then again before GitHub label/PR writes.
callisto release-pr verify --decision "$decision" --snapshot "$(release_pr_snapshot)" > /dev/null

if gh api -X PATCH "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs/heads/$staging_branch" -f sha="$base_commit" -F force=true > /dev/null 2>&1; then
  :
else
  gh api -X POST "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs" -f ref="refs/heads/$staging_branch" -f sha="$base_commit" > /dev/null
fi
staging_created=true

jq -n \
  --arg repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
  --arg branch "$staging_branch" \
  --arg headline "$INPUT_COMMIT_MESSAGE" \
  --slurpfile plan "$plan_file" \
  '{
    query: "mutation($input: CreateCommitOnBranchInput!) { createCommitOnBranch(input: $input) { commit { oid } } }",
    variables: {
      input: {
        branch: {repositoryNameWithOwner: $repo, branchName: $branch},
        message: {headline: $headline},
        expectedHeadOid: $plan[0].baseCommit,
        fileChanges: {
          additions: [$plan[0].additions[] | {path, contents: .contentsBase64}],
          deletions: $plan[0].deletions
        }
      }
    }
  }' > body.json

new_sha=$(gh api graphql --input body.json --jq '.data.createCommitOnBranch.commit.oid')
remote_tree=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/commits/$new_sha" --jq '.tree.sha')
if [[ "$remote_tree" != "$local_tree" ]]; then
  echo "::error::forge commit tree $remote_tree does not match the locally staged tree $local_tree; refusing to move $release_branch"
  exit 1
fi

callisto release-pr verify --decision "$decision" --snapshot "$(release_pr_snapshot)" > /dev/null

if [[ "$decision_kind" == update ]]; then
  gh api -X PATCH "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs/heads/$release_branch" -f sha="$new_sha" -F force=true > /dev/null
else
  if ! gh api -X POST "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs" -f ref="refs/heads/$release_branch" -f sha="$new_sha" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
    gh api -X PATCH "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs/heads/$release_branch" -f sha="$new_sha" -F force=true > /dev/null
  fi
fi
moved_sha=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs/heads/$release_branch" --jq '.object.sha')
if [[ "$moved_sha" != "$new_sha" ]]; then
  echo "::error::$release_branch points at $moved_sha after the update, expected $new_sha; a concurrent write may have raced this run"
  exit 1
fi

callisto release-pr verify --decision "$decision" --snapshot "$(release_pr_snapshot)" > /dev/null

label_exists=$(gh label list --limit 1000 --json name --jq 'any(.[]; .name == env.INPUT_PR_LABEL)')
if [[ "$label_exists" != true ]]; then
  gh label create "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" --color 0e8a16 --description 'Callisto release packages'
fi

case "$decision_kind" in
  create)
    gh pr create --head "$release_branch" --base "$INPUT_BRANCH" --title "$INPUT_TITLE" --body "$body" --label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL"
    ;;
  update)
    gh pr edit "$existing_pr" --title "$INPUT_TITLE" --body "$body" --add-label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL"
    ;;
esac
