export const meta = {
  name: 'error-taxonomy-architecture-proposals',
  description: 'Design structural fixes for the ReleaseIntentStale catch-all and workspace-wide error-source erasure',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Recon', detail: 'catalogue every error-source-erasure site (low-cost enumeration)' },
    { title: 'Propose', detail: 'architect a spec@1 for each defect class' },
  ],
}

const WORKSPACE_ROOT = '/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto'

// Already established in a prior investigation this session (an agent read
// every GraphError::ReleaseIntentStale construction site directly) -- reused
// verbatim here instead of re-deriving it, to avoid burning a second
// investigation pass on the same 83 sites.
const RELEASE_INTENT_STALE_FINDING = `
GraphError::ReleaseIntentStale is constructed at 83 sites across 3 files in callisto-graph:
crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release.rs (~60 sites), release_decision.rs (~40 sites,
including the recently-added git-cat-file-batch verification path), release_execution.rs
(2 sites). Its #[diagnostic(help)] text reads: "Regenerate and reapprove the release intent;
no release operation was authorized." It is nearly the only error variant release.rs uses --
39 "return Err(GraphError::...)" sites in that file alone, with ReleaseIntentStale accounting
for the overwhelming majority, versus 6 distinct variants total.

Confirmed distinct failure families currently collapsed onto this one variant, each with
concrete evidence from live code:

1. Genuinely correct uses (~8-10 sites): pre-dispatch re-observation of git trust/workspace
   state changing between reads (recheck_trust, build_release_intent,
   validate_release_intent_with_state_directory in release.rs). Staleness is the real cause.

2. Post-dispatch mischaracterization (release.rs ~line 367, dispatch_registry): fires when an
   npm publish command already succeeded but the registry has not yet caught up
   (!self.npm_version_is_published(...)). "No release operation was authorized" is factually
   false here -- an operation WAS authorized and executed; the real issue is registry
   propagation lag. This is a standalone, well-isolated bug independent of the wider taxonomy
   problem -- it's the one site an operator could be actively misled by today.

3. Git/subprocess command failures (release_decision.rs ~line 255, git_stdout; similar sites
   in release.rs for git push / gh release create / gh api): any non-zero exit from
   rev-parse/diff-tree/show/push/gh becomes "release intent stale," discarding the actual
   subprocess failure (auth failure, network error, merge conflict, rate limit, etc).

4. Parse/deserialize failures: malformed CommitSha, malformed git name-status output,
   malformed JSON (decision file, GitHub API response), malformed manifest version -- all
   folded into the same variant regardless of what failed to parse.

5. Commit-provenance/verification mismatches in derive_release_commit_decision (the function
   this session's F20 fix touched): "decision file not freshly written," "no changeset
   consumed," "changelog path not touched," "manifest version doesn't match claim,"
   "unauthorized version change" -- each is a distinct, nameable verification failure against
   an ALREADY-MERGED commit, so "regenerate and reapprove the release intent" is nonsensical
   guidance at this call site specifically (there is no intent left to reapprove; the commit
   already landed).

6. Unsupported/unreachable match arms: unsupported ecosystem, HermeticContent source variant,
   unhandled future BumpReason variants in reason_from_bump's catch-all -- "unhandled case,"
   not staleness.

7. Config/invariant errors: no canonical manifest format for an ecosystem, cascade
   via-package identity lookup failure.

Notably, release.rs already demonstrates the correct pattern exists and is known:
ReleasePackageNotSelected { package } (diagnostic code E123) is a properly distinct,
accurately-worded variant used at exactly one site (derive_release_inputs) -- proving the
team already knows how to do this right elsewhere in the same file; ReleaseIntentStale was
simply the path of least resistance everywhere else.

A prior investigating agent's suggested phasing (not binding, offered as a starting point):
(a) fix the standalone post-dispatch bug (family 2) as its own tiny hotfix, independent of
the rest; (b) release_execution.rs's 2 sites next (smallest, cleanest -- "artifact manifest
required" vs "artifact manifest mismatch," clearly distinct from staleness); (c)
release_decision.rs's derive_release_commit_decision next (self-contained verification
function, ~30 sites, plausibly mappable to a ReleaseCommitVerificationFailed{reason}-shaped
variant or similar); (d) release.rs's dispatch/observation layer last (largest, most
delicate, includes family 2's site).
`

const EROSION_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    total_confirmed_sites: { type: 'number' },
    categories: {
      type: 'array',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        properties: {
          name: { type: 'string' },
          count: { type: 'number' },
          shape: { type: 'string', description: 'the exact code shape, e.g. map_err(|_err| ...) with the binding never read' },
          representative_examples: {
            type: 'array',
            items: {
              type: 'object',
              properties: {
                file: { type: 'string' },
                line: { type: 'number' },
                discarded_cause: { type: 'string' },
                folded_into: { type: 'string' },
                harm: { type: 'string', description: 'concrete operator-facing harm, or "benign" with justification' },
              },
              required: ['file', 'line', 'discarded_cause', 'folded_into', 'harm'],
            },
          },
        },
        required: ['name', 'count', 'shape', 'representative_examples'],
      },
    },
    worst_crates: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    systemic_fix_warranted: { type: 'boolean' },
    systemic_fix_rationale: { type: 'string' },
  },
  required: ['total_confirmed_sites', 'categories', 'systemic_fix_warranted', 'systemic_fix_rationale'],
}

const PROPOSAL_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    problem: { type: 'string', description: 'concrete, evidence-grounded statement of the defect class -- what is actually broken today, with real examples' },
    why_it_matters: { type: 'string', description: 'the operator- or maintainer-facing consequence; who gets hurt and how, not abstract code-quality language' },
    proposal: { type: 'string', description: 'the structural change: new types/variants/traits/lints that make the defect class impossible or unrepresentable, not a per-instance patch list' },
    outcome: { type: 'string', description: 'what becomes true after the fix ships -- observable, testable end-state' },
    spec: {
      type: 'object',
      description: 'a spec@1-shaped artifact for this change',
      properties: {
        id: { type: 'string' },
        purpose: { type: 'string' },
        scope: { type: 'string' },
        non_goals: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
        acceptance_criteria: {
          type: 'array',
          items: {
            type: 'object',
            properties: {
              id: { type: 'string' },
              criterion: { type: 'string' },
              is_error_case: { type: 'boolean' },
            },
            required: ['id', 'criterion'],
          },
        },
      },
      required: ['id', 'purpose', 'scope', 'acceptance_criteria'],
    },
    estimated_blast_radius: { type: 'string', description: 'files/sites touched, rough scale' },
  },
  required: ['problem', 'why_it_matters', 'proposal', 'outcome', 'spec'],
}

log('Cataloguing error-source-erasure sites across the workspace...')

const erasureRecon = await agent(
  `Enumerate every site in the Rust workspace at ${WORKSPACE_ROOT} (crates/*/src/**/*.rs, excluding #[cfg(test)] modules and test files) where an error's real underlying cause is discarded before being folded into a new, less-specific error.

Patterns to search, in order of expected volume:
1. ".map_err(|_| ...)" / ".map_err(|_err| ...)" / ".map_err(|_error| ...)" / ".map_err(|_e| ...)" / ".map_err(|_grammar_mismatch| ...)" etc. -- any map_err closure whose bound parameter is never referenced in its body. A quick grep for "map_err(|_" across crates/*/src already surfaced 42+ hits; read each one in context to confirm the binding is truly unused (not, e.g., matched via a guard) and to capture what the discarded value actually was.
2. ".ok()" called on a Result (not Option) that silently discards the Err payload, where that Err carried real diagnostic information -- distinguish this from legitimate uses where an error genuinely does not matter (e.g. probing whether an optional file exists).
3. Catch-all match arms shaped "_ => Err(SomeGenericVariant)" or "_ => Err(SomeGenericVariant { .. })" that fold two or more textually-distinct upstream failure causes into one undifferentiated downstream error, losing the ability to tell them apart later.
4. A new error type that wraps an inner Result's Err without preserving it as a #[source] or #[from] in a thiserror/miette-style enum, when the inner error type already implements std::error::Error and a proper source chain would be straightforward.

For each pattern, read the surrounding function to understand what specific information is actually being lost, and make a genuine judgment call about harm: does an operator debugging a real failure lose actionable information (the specific reason a git command failed, which field failed to parse, which of several possible causes triggered this branch), or is the erasure inconsequential because the underlying cause realistically only has one shape in practice? Do not pad the count with trivial matches -- a map_err that discards a truly interchangeable error (e.g. collapsing two variants of the same "not found" condition that are handled identically downstream) is not harmful erasure.

Group findings into a small number of named categories by root cause/shape (not one row per site) with representative examples (5-10 total across all categories, prioritizing the most harmful). Report which crates concentrate the worst offenders, a total confirmed count, and a clear judgment on whether this pattern is a "systemic" problem warranting a structural fix (a clippy lint rule forbidding it, a macro/helper that makes preserving the source easier than discarding it, a documented workspace-wide convention with enforcement) versus something better handled as scattered per-site patches. Be rigorous and skeptical of your own count -- state your reasoning for what you included and excluded.`,
  { phase: 'Recon', effort: 'high', schema: EROSION_SCHEMA }
)

log(`Recon complete: ${erasureRecon.total_confirmed_sites} confirmed error-source-erasure sites across ${erasureRecon.categories.length} categories. Designing both proposals in parallel...`)

const [staleProposal, erasureProposal] = await parallel([
  () =>
    agent(
      `You are designing a structural fix for a confirmed defect class in the Callisto Rust monorepo (workspace root ${WORKSPACE_ROOT}), a release/versioning engine. Read the current code at the referenced files/lines yourself to ground your proposal in what is actually there today -- do not take the finding below as a substitute for reading the real code, use it as your investigation starting point and verify/deepen it.

CONFIRMED FINDING (from a prior investigation this session):

[package]
name = "callisto-moon"
version = "0.6.0"
edition.workspace = true
license = "AGPL-3.0-only"
description = "Callisto Release Engine — Moon WASM PDK plugin for polyglot monorepo release automation."
repository.workspace = true
readme = "README.md"

# No [lib] crate-type = ["cdylib", ...] here deliberately: declaring cdylib
# in the manifest makes cargo build a native cdylib artifact too whenever the
# "pdk" feature is enabled (e.g. `cargo llvm-cov --all-features` on macOS),
# and that native link fails -- the pdk-feature code references extism-pdk's
# WASM-host-only import symbols (_alloc, _input_length, etc.), which don't
# exist for native linking. The wasm32-wasip1 cdylib artifact is instead
# requested explicitly, only for that target, via `cargo rustc --crate-type
# cdylib` in `just wasm-check` and in tests/moon_wasm_sandbox.rs's build step.

[features]
default = []
pdk = [
    "dep:extism-pdk",
    "dep:moon_pdk_api",
    "dep:moon_pdk",
    "dep:warpgate_pdk",
    "dep:schematic",
    "dep:schematic_types",
]
# Spike: track whether gix low-level plumbing crates can read a real git repo
# from inside a WASM guest via WASI filesystem preopens. Gates the
# examples/gix_wasm_spike.rs binary only -- never enabled in the shipped wasm.
gix-spike = ["dep:gix-odb", "dep:gix-ref", "dep:gix-hash"]

[dependencies]
callisto-model = { path = "../callisto-model", version = "0.6.0" }
callisto-graph = { path = "../callisto-graph", version = "0.6.0" }
serde = { workspace = true }
serde_json = { workspace = true }
semver = { workspace = true }
extism-pdk = { version = "1.4.1", optional = true }
gix-hash = { version = "0.26", optional = true }
gix-odb = { version = "0.83", optional = true }
gix-ref = { version = "0.66", optional = true }
moon_pdk_api = { version = "2.0.4", optional = true }
moon_pdk = { version = "2.0.4", optional = true }
# Pinned to the version moon v2.4.6 / moon_pdk_api 2.0.4 actually resolve to
# in this workspace's Cargo.lock (0.16.5) so no duplicate major/minor
# resolution occurs alongside the transitive copy pulled in by moon_pdk_api.
warpgate_pdk = { version = "0.16.5", optional = true }
# Pinned to the version moon_pdk_api 2.0.4 actually resolves to in this
# workspace's Cargo.lock (0.19.7); needed directly (not just transitively) to
# construct `moon_pdk_api::DefineExtensionConfigOutput`'s `schema: Schema`
# field. Features mirror moon_pdk_api's own `schematic` dependency features
# exactly (see its Cargo.toml) so no duplicate/mismatched feature resolution
# occurs alongside the transitive copy it pulls in.
schematic = { version = "0.19.7", optional = true, default-features = false, features = [
    "schema",
    "schema_serde",
] }
# Pinned to the exact `schematic_types` version `schematic` 0.19.7 resolves
# to in this workspace's Cargo.lock (0.11.5); `schematic` re-exports
# `Schema`/`SchemaType` from this crate but not the individual type-shape
# structs (e.g. `StructType`), which `define_extension_config` needs to
# construct an empty-object schema directly.
schematic_types = { version = "0.11.5", optional = true }

[dev-dependencies]
# Process-global test-observability counters (callisto_graph::identity's
# identity_read_count) are shared across all tests in one binary; #[serial]
# keeps a counting regression test from racing sibling tests in the same file.

# into a real wasmtime-backed extism plugin container (via warpgate) and
# drives register_extension/execute_extension through the actual Extism
# wire protocol, instead of only type-checking the Rust source. Requires
# `callisto-moon.wasm` to already be built for wasm32-wasip1 with the
# `pdk` feature (see `just wasm-check`) before running `cargo test`.
moon_pdk_test_utils = "2.0.4"
# `moon_pdk_api` (re-exported by `moon_pdk_test_utils`) does not re-export
# `schematic`'s types; needed directly to assert on
# `DefineExtensionConfigOutput.schema`'s `SchemaType` shape in

schematic_types = "0.11.5"

[package]
name = "callisto-moon"
version = "0.6.0"
edition.workspace = true
license = "AGPL-3.0-only"
description = "Callisto Release Engine — Moon WASM PDK plugin for polyglot monorepo release automation."
repository.workspace = true
readme = "README.md"

[lints]
workspace = true

# No [lib] crate-type = ["cdylib", ...] here deliberately: declaring cdylib
# in the manifest makes cargo build a native cdylib artifact too whenever the
# "pdk" feature is enabled (e.g. `cargo llvm-cov --all-features` on macOS),
# and that native link fails -- the pdk-feature code references extism-pdk's
# WASM-host-only import symbols (_alloc, _input_length, etc.), which don't
# exist for native linking. The wasm32-wasip1 cdylib artifact is instead
# requested explicitly, only for that target, via `cargo rustc --crate-type
# cdylib` in `just wasm-check` and in tests/moon_wasm_sandbox.rs's build step.

[features]
default = []
pdk = [
    "dep:extism-pdk",
    "dep:moon_pdk_api",
    "dep:moon_pdk",
    "dep:warpgate_pdk",
    "dep:schematic",
    "dep:schematic_types",
]
# Spike: track whether gix low-level plumbing crates can read a real git repo
# from inside a WASM guest via WASI filesystem preopens. Gates the
# examples/gix_wasm_spike.rs binary only -- never enabled in the shipped wasm.
gix-spike = ["dep:gix-odb", "dep:gix-ref", "dep:gix-hash"]

[dependencies]
callisto-model = { path = "../callisto-model", version = "0.6.0" }
callisto-graph = { path = "../callisto-graph", version = "0.6.0" }
serde = { workspace = true }
serde_json = { workspace = true }
semver = { workspace = true }
extism-pdk = { version = "1.4.1", optional = true }
gix-hash = { version = "0.26", optional = true }
gix-odb = { version = "0.83", optional = true }
gix-ref = { version = "0.66", optional = true }
moon_pdk_api = { version = "2.0.4", optional = true }
moon_pdk = { version = "2.0.4", optional = true }
# Pinned to the version moon v2.4.6 / moon_pdk_api 2.0.4 actually resolve to
# in this workspace's Cargo.lock (0.16.5) so no duplicate major/minor
# resolution occurs alongside the transitive copy pulled in by moon_pdk_api.
warpgate_pdk = { version = "0.16.5", optional = true }
# Pinned to the version moon_pdk_api 2.0.4 actually resolves to in this
# workspace's Cargo.lock (0.19.7); needed directly (not just transitively) to
# construct `moon_pdk_api::DefineExtensionConfigOutput`'s `schema: Schema`
# field. Features mirror moon_pdk_api's own `schematic` dependency features
# exactly (see its Cargo.toml) so no duplicate/mismatched feature resolution
# occurs alongside the transitive copy it pulls in.
schematic = { version = "0.19.7", optional = true, default-features = false, features = [
    "schema",
    "schema_serde",
] }
# Pinned to the exact `schematic_types` version `schematic` 0.19.7 resolves
# to in this workspace's Cargo.lock (0.11.5); `schematic` re-exports
# `Schema`/`SchemaType` from this crate but not the individual type-shape
# structs (e.g. `StructType`), which `define_extension_config` needs to
# construct an empty-object schema directly.
schematic_types = { version = "0.11.5", optional = true }

[dev-dependencies]
# Process-global test-observability counters (callisto_graph::identity's
# identity_read_count) are shared across all tests in one binary; #[serial]
# keeps a counting regression test from racing sibling tests in the same file.
serial_test.workspace = true
# Black-box protocol verification: loads the *compiled* callisto-moon.wasm
# into a real wasmtime-backed extism plugin container (via warpgate) and
# drives register_extension/execute_extension through the actual Extism
# wire protocol, instead of only type-checking the Rust source. Requires
# `callisto-moon.wasm` to already be built for wasm32-wasip1 with the
# `pdk` feature (see `just wasm-check`) before running `cargo test`.
moon_pdk_test_utils = "2.0.4"
# `moon_pdk_api` (re-exported by `moon_pdk_test_utils`) does not re-export
# `schematic`'s types; needed directly to assert on
# `DefineExtensionConfigOutput.schema`'s `SchemaType` shape in
# `tests/moon_wasm_sandbox.rs`. Version left unpinned (unlike the `pdk`-gated

# Fixture repo staging for the strengthened `execute_extension` sandbox

# to the newer patch. Pin the transitive resolution back to the last
# version where the default features still include it.

[package]
name = "callisto-moon"
version = "0.6.0"
edition.workspace = true
license = "AGPL-3.0-only"
description = "Callisto Release Engine — Moon WASM PDK plugin for polyglot monorepo release automation."
repository.workspace = true
readme = "README.md"

# Not `[lints]\nworkspace = true`: this crate's tests/moon_wasm_sandbox.rs
# mutates process-wide env vars (WARPGATE_PLUGINS_DIR, PATH) under a
# `Once`/`PATH_MUTEX`-serialized, individually SAFETY-commented `unsafe`
# block per call, which the workspace's `unsafe_code = "forbid"` cannot
# locally allow (forbid, unlike deny, can't be overridden by any in-source
# attribute, at any nesting depth). Clippy lints still inherit unchanged;
# only the rust-lint table's unsafe_code is downgraded to "deny" so this
# crate keeps "unsafe fails the build by default everywhere," while still
# permitting this one reviewed, narrowly-scoped exception via a local
# #[allow(unsafe_code)] at each site.
[lints.clippy]
workspace = true

[lints.rust]
unsafe_code = "deny"
unused_must_use = "deny"
let_underscore_drop = "deny"

# No [lib] crate-type = ["cdylib", ...] here deliberately: declaring cdylib
# in the manifest makes cargo build a native cdylib artifact too whenever the
# "pdk" feature is enabled (e.g. `cargo llvm-cov --all-features` on macOS),
# and that native link fails -- the pdk-feature code references extism-pdk's
# WASM-host-only import symbols (_alloc, _input_length, etc.), which don't
# exist for native linking. The wasm32-wasip1 cdylib artifact is instead
# requested explicitly, only for that target, via `cargo rustc --crate-type
# cdylib` in `just wasm-check` and in tests/moon_wasm_sandbox.rs's build step.

[features]
default = []
pdk = [
    "dep:extism-pdk",
    "dep:moon_pdk_api",
    "dep:moon_pdk",
    "dep:warpgate_pdk",
    "dep:schematic",
    "dep:schematic_types",
]
# Spike: track whether gix low-level plumbing crates can read a real git repo
# from inside a WASM guest via WASI filesystem preopens. Gates the
# examples/gix_wasm_spike.rs binary only -- never enabled in the shipped wasm.
gix-spike = ["dep:gix-odb", "dep:gix-ref", "dep:gix-hash"]

[dependencies]
callisto-model = { path = "../callisto-model", version = "0.6.0" }
callisto-graph = { path = "../callisto-graph", version = "0.6.0" }
serde = { workspace = true }
serde_json = { workspace = true }
semver = { workspace = true }
extism-pdk = { version = "1.4.1", optional = true }
gix-hash = { version = "0.26", optional = true }
gix-odb = { version = "0.83", optional = true }
gix-ref = { version = "0.66", optional = true }
moon_pdk_api = { version = "2.0.4", optional = true }
moon_pdk = { version = "2.0.4", optional = true }
# Pinned to the version moon v2.4.6 / moon_pdk_api 2.0.4 actually resolve to
# in this workspace's Cargo.lock (0.16.5) so no duplicate major/minor
# resolution occurs alongside the transitive copy pulled in by moon_pdk_api.
warpgate_pdk = { version = "0.16.5", optional = true }
# Pinned to the version moon_pdk_api 2.0.4 actually resolves to in this
# workspace's Cargo.lock (0.19.7); needed directly (not just transitively) to
# construct `moon_pdk_api::DefineExtensionConfigOutput`'s `schema: Schema`
# field. Features mirror moon_pdk_api's own `schematic` dependency features
# exactly (see its Cargo.toml) so no duplicate/mismatched feature resolution
# occurs alongside the transitive copy it pulls in.
schematic = { version = "0.19.7", optional = true, default-features = false, features = [
    "schema",
    "schema_serde",
] }
# Pinned to the exact `schematic_types` version `schematic` 0.19.7 resolves
# to in this workspace's Cargo.lock (0.11.5); `schematic` re-exports
# `Schema`/`SchemaType` from this crate but not the individual type-shape
# structs (e.g. `StructType`), which `define_extension_config` needs to
# construct an empty-object schema directly.
schematic_types = { version = "0.11.5", optional = true }

[dev-dependencies]
# Process-global test-observability counters (callisto_graph::identity's
# identity_read_count) are shared across all tests in one binary; #[serial]
# keeps a counting regression test from racing sibling tests in the same file.
serial_test.workspace = true
# Black-box protocol verification: loads the *compiled* callisto-moon.wasm
# into a real wasmtime-backed extism plugin container (via warpgate) and
# drives register_extension/execute_extension through the actual Extism
# wire protocol, instead of only type-checking the Rust source. Requires
# `callisto-moon.wasm` to already be built for wasm32-wasip1 with the
# `pdk` feature (see `just wasm-check`) before running `cargo test`.
moon_pdk_test_utils = "2.0.4"
# `moon_pdk_api` (re-exported by `moon_pdk_test_utils`) does not re-export
# `schematic`'s types; needed directly to assert on
# `DefineExtensionConfigOutput.schema`'s `SchemaType` shape in
# `tests/moon_wasm_sandbox.rs`. Version left unpinned (unlike the `pdk`-gated
# main-dependency copy) since dev-dependencies don't affect the shipped wasm
# artifact's dependency resolution.
schematic_types = "0.11.5"
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["macros", "rt-multi-thread", "sync"] }
# Fixture repo staging for the strengthened `execute_extension` sandbox
# regression test (real `git init` + tagged commit under a scratch dir).
tempfile = { workspace = true }
# Pin: warpgate 0.30.5 (a moon_pdk_test_utils 2.0.4 transitive dependency)
# requests `http-cache-reqwest = "1.0.0-alpha.5"` but does not request the
# `manager-cacache` feature it actually needs (`CACacheManager`). That
# feature was default-on through 1.0.0-alpha.6 and became opt-in in
# 1.0.0-alpha.7, which breaks warpgate's build when the workspace resolves
# to the newer patch. Pin the transitive resolution back to the last
# version where the default features still include it.
http-cache-reqwest = "=1.0.0-alpha.6"

**Batch `WorkspaceCargoResolver`-routed writes to a shared root `Cargo.toml` into one open/mutate/persist cycle**

`WorkspaceCargoResolver::write_version`/`write_dependency` in `callisto-manifests` no longer call `persist` internally -- they now do pure in-memory mutation only, mirroring the `Manifest` trait's `write_version`/`update_dependency_spec`/`persist` split already used by `CargoToml`/`PackageJson`/`PyprojectToml`. `persist` is promoted to a public, explicitly-called method. Every existing call site (the inherited-dependency delegation inside `CargoToml::update_dependency_spec`, and both of `apply_version_plan`'s per-write fallback loops) now calls `persist` explicitly afterward -- no behavior change there.

`callisto-graph`'s `classify_manifest_writes`/`apply_version_plan` (`apply.rs`) now route root-manifest writes (`VersionWriteTarget::CargoWorkspacePackage`/`DepWriteTarget::CargoWorkspaceDependency`) into a new `resolver_batched` group when the same physical root manifest receives no competing write through the `Manifest` trait. A release that bumps the workspace version plus several workspace-inherited dependencies now opens the root `Cargo.toml` once, applies every mutation in memory, and persists exactly once -- down from one read+parse+atomic-write per write. The pre-existing mixed-routing exclusion (a root manifest written through *both* the `Manifest` trait and `WorkspaceCargoResolver` -- the data-loss/ordering hazard `classify_manifest_writes` already guarded against) is unchanged: those paths still get no batching on either side, processed individually and in the same order as before.

New `resolver_load_call_count`/`resolver_persist_call_count` test-observability counters (kept separate from `open_call_count`/`persist_call_count`, since `OpenContext::for_workspace_root` calls `WorkspaceCargoResolver::load` unconditionally whenever a workspace root `Cargo.toml` exists, which would otherwise pollute those counters workspace-wide) prove the new batched path opens and persists the shared root manifest exactly once per `apply_version_plan` call, regardless of how many bumps/rewrites target it, while the mixed-routing case continues to persist each write individually.

content.text:
Both design proposals are done and saved as spec files (`.claude/specs/SPEC-ARCH-RELEASE-ERROR-TAXONOMY.json` and `SPEC-ARCH-ERROR-SOURCE-PRESERVATION-GATE.json`). Two independent `scribe:architect` passes converged on the same root cause from different angles, so here's both, plus how they relate.

## #2 — The `ReleaseIntentStale` catch-all

**Problem.** `GraphError::ReleaseIntentStale` (E124, help: "no release operation was authorized") is constructed at **101 sites**, not the 83 originally estimated — a deeper read found more. Only **6 are genuine staleness**. The other 95 discard a real, already-typed cause: registry errors (rate limits, auth failures), non-zero git/gh subprocess exits with stderr thrown away, ~15 distinct merged-commit verification mismatches, remote-object conflicts (tag/release already exists elsewhere), and internal invariants — all rendered as the identical message.

**Why it matters.** For 95 of 101 failure paths, an operator or CI job is told to "regenerate and reapprove the release intent" when that's not just unhelpful — for a rejected `git push`, an expired npm token, or a tag conflict, it's actively wrong. This has already been silently patched twice (E136, E157) by bolting on a sibling variant; the unit variant is still the path of least resistance for every next contributor.

**Proposal.** Make staleness itself a proof-carrying variant that only the observation code can construct (module-private `StaleReason`), give every other family its own typed variant (14 new error codes, E158–E171) fed by `?` instead of `map_err`, and enforce it with architecture tests (a source-scan for the `map_err(|_ident|)` evasion, a check that `ReleaseIntentStale` compiles only in 4 named functions). Sequenced as 4 independently-shippable PRs with a deprecation-ratchet so migration progress can only go forward.

**Outcome.** Every release failure surfaces its real cause and real next action — a rate limit says "retry after Ns," a tag conflict names both SHAs, a rejected commit names which of 15 checks failed. `just lint` passes with zero new `#[allow]`s.

## #3 — Error-source erasure (workspace-wide)

**Problem.** The workspace already set `clippy::map_err_ignore = "deny"` — but the lint only catches the bare `|_|` closure. The codebase converged on `|_error|`/`|_err|`/`|_e|` instead (42 sites, 16 files, 7 crates), which discards the cause identically while evading the guard rail that was supposed to stop it. This is the *same underlying defect* as #2, just measured workspace-wide instead of scoped to the release path — the recon agent flagged 28 of its 40 confirmed sites as being exactly `ReleaseIntentStale`'s sink.

**Why it matters.** A `moon.yml` parse error and a missing `moon` binary render identically, discarding moon's own actionable stderr. A malformed `--repository` flag says the string is wrong without saying what's wrong about it. A read-only release-state directory reports "could not create directory" with zero indication of why.

**Proposal.** One CI/`just lint` gate script (matching this repo's existing `.github/tests/*.sh` convention) that rejects the `|_ident|` evasion spelling and any `#[allow(clippy::map_err_ignore)]`, funneling every future attempt onto the bare `|_|` the existing lint already catches — with `#[expect(..., reason = "...")]` as the sole, reviewable escape hatch. Plus `#[source]` slots on the handful of sibling error types (`VcsError`, `LocateError`, `ConfigError`) that structurally can't carry a cause today.

**Outcome.** `rg 'map_err\(\s*\|_[A-Za-z_]' crates/` goes from 42 to 0, permanently, enforced in CI. **Coordination note:** this gate's regex also matches the 42-of-101 release-path sites #2 migrates — land the gate's CI wiring only after #2's PR1 lands its own ratchet, or the two will fight over the same lines mid-migration.

Both are drafts for your review, not yet implemented. Want me to start #2's PR1 (the foundational error.rs taxonomy + architecture tests, no behavior change), or scope something smaller first?

input.prompt:
You are implementing PR1 of a 4-PR migration in the Callisto Rust monorepo (a release/versioning engine), fixing a confirmed architectural defect: `GraphError::ReleaseIntentStale` is a fieldless unit variant constructed at ~100 sites in `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/{release.rs,release_decision.rs,release_execution.rs}`, but only 6 of those sites are genuine staleness — the rest silently discard a real, already-typed failure cause and report the same generic, often-misleading message. This has already caused real operator confusion (documented in the spec).

Read the full design spec first: `.claude/specs/SPEC-ARCH-RELEASE-ERROR-TAXONOMY.json` in the repo root. It has the complete problem statement, all acceptance criteria, and a `suggested_pr_sequence` field — you are implementing exactly `suggested_pr_sequence[0]` (PR1), nothing more. Do NOT implement PR2/PR3/PR4's scope (wiring E163-E171 into actual call sites) — that's deliberately deferred to later PRs.

IMPORTANT environment note: a global RTK hook rewrites bare `git` to `rtk git`, which breaks inside worktree-isolated agents. Use `/usr/bin/git` (or `/opt/homebrew/bin/git`) explicitly for every git command. If you hit a *different* permission-classifier denial after that workaround (not the git-rewrite one), STOP — do not retry alternate forms, do not touch rtk config — leave edits uncommitted and report back to me so I can commit from my own session.

You're on top of an existing branch (`feat/release-intent-stale-taxonomy-pr1`, based on a not-yet-merged PR that added a related `RegistryPublishUnconfirmed` (E157) variant to the same `error.rs`/`release.rs` files — read the current state of those files fresh, do not assume line numbers from the spec are still accurate; the spec's site counts were computed before that PR's changes, so re-derive exact current counts and locations yourself by reading the code, don't trust the spec's numbers as literal line references (its qualitative content — which sites are genuine staleness vs. discarded-cause — is still accurate; only line numbers may have drifted).

## Exact PR1 scope

1. **Add every new error variant and reason enum to `crates/callisto-graph/src/error.rs`** exactly as specified in the spec's `proposal` field and AC-004 through AC-013 (codes E158 through E171 — continue numbering from whatever the current highest diagnostic code actually is in the file, verify it yourself, don't assume E157 is the max since PR #78 might not be the only recent addition). Each new variant needs an accurate `#[error(...)]` message, a `#[diagnostic(code(E1xx), help(...))]` with real, non-generic help text specific to that failure family (not a copy of E124's text), and a `#[source]` field where it wraps an upstream error type. None of these new variants need to be constructed anywhere yet in this PR except where specified in step 3 below — that's fine, they won't trigger dead-code warnings since `GraphError` is a `pub` enum.

2. **Flip `GraphError::ReleaseIntentStale` from a unit variant to a struct variant** `ReleaseIntentStale { reason: StaleReason }`, keeping its existing diagnostic code (E124) and help text unchanged, but update its `#[error(...)]` Display message to append the reason, e.g. `"release intent no longer matches the current workspace snapshot: {reason}"`.

3. **Define `StaleReason` in `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release.rs`** (NOT in error.rs) as a `pub struct StaleReason` with a private inner field (e.g. a private `kind: StaleKind` enum, or whatever internal shape you judge cleanest) and exactly these constructor functions, each with NO visibility modifier (not `pub`, not `pub(crate)`, not `pub(super)` — fully private, callable only from within `release.rs` itself):
   - `trust_evidence_changed()`
   - `source_identity_changed()`
   - `git_remote_changed()`
   - `intent_differs_from_fresh_derivation()`
   Give `StaleReason` a `Display` impl (and whatever derives `GraphError` needs it to have — check what `GraphError` itself derives, e.g. `Clone`, `PartialEq`, `Eq`, and match that).

content.content:
---
callisto-graph: minor
---

**`GraphError::ReleaseIntentStale` (E124) becomes a struct variant carrying a real reason**

PR1 of a 4-PR migration (SPEC-ARCH-RELEASE-ERROR-TAXONOMY) fixing a confirmed architectural defect: `ReleaseIntentStale` was a fieldless unit variant constructed at ~95 sites across `commands/{release.rs,release_decision.rs,release_execution.rs}`, of which only 6 were genuine staleness -- the rest silently discarded an already-typed failure cause (a model error, a subprocess exit status, a merged-commit verification mismatch, a remote conflict, and more) behind the same generic, sometimes misleading "no release operation was authorized" message.

- `ReleaseIntentStale` is now `{ reason: StaleReason }`; its Display message appends the reason, and its diagnostic code/help text are unchanged. This is semver-breaking for any external consumer pattern-matching the old unit variant (none exist inside this workspace).
- `StaleReason` (`callisto-graph::commands::release`) is nameable everywhere but constructible with a real reason only from within `release.rs` itself -- `trust_evidence_changed`, `source_identity_changed`, `git_remote_changed`, and `intent_differs_from_fresh_derivation` cover the module's 6 genuine fresh-re-observation sites. Every other prior `ReleaseIntentStale` site (44 in `release.rs`, 42 in `release_decision.rs`, 2 in `release_execution.rs`) now uses a temporary, `#[deprecated]`, `pub(crate)` `StaleReason::legacy_unclassified()` migration ratchet, pinned exactly by a new architecture test and lowered to zero across PR2-PR4 as each site is given its real cause.
- Twelve new `GraphError` variants (E158-E171) give a typed home to every previously-discarded cause -- model construction errors, registry failures, subprocess command failures, merged-commit verification mismatches, remote conflicts, unsupported feature combinations, invalid selections, unmet preconditions, and internal invariants -- ready for PR2-PR4 to wire into their real call sites.
- New architecture tests in `crates/callisto-graph/tests/architecture.rs` enforce the module-privacy boundary, pin the ratchet counts, guard against new `map_err(|_ident| ...)` source-discarding closures elsewhere in the crate, and confirm E124's "reapprove" guidance isn't copied onto any of the new variants.

No behavior change beyond E124's Display text gaining a reason suffix.

lastPrompt: Should we enable merge queing to avoid this sync branch madness?

content.text:
No — merge queue wouldn't have prevented this. The cause was different: I deliberately based PR #79's branch on PR #78's branch (since they touched overlapping lines in `error.rs`), and this repo squash-merges. Squash-merge always rewrites the merged PR's commits into one new commit — so *any* branch stacked on top of it needs a rebase once it merges, regardless of merge queue. Merge queue serializes and pre-tests merges into `main`; it doesn't manage relationships between stacked branches at all.

What would actually reduce this:
- **Avoid stacking on unmerged PR branches** when the overlap is small — basing on `main` and resolving one manual conflict at PR-open time is usually less friction than a rebase-after-squash later. That's the mistake here, not a missing repo setting.
- **"Require branches to be up to date before merging"** (a branch-protection setting, separate from merge queue) would have caught this immediately rather than letting it surface as a mid-flight conflict — worth turning on regardless.
- **Merge queue** earns its keep when several PRs are merging in quick succession and you want each tested against the *actual* post-merge state before landing (catches semantic conflicts a single PR's own CI can't see). Given the volume here is one session merging PRs sequentially, it's not solving a problem you currently have — but it's a reasonable hardening if PR throughput picks up.

Want me to just default to basing new work on `main` going forward (only stacking when a PR is genuinely blocked on unmerged code), or set up branch protection's "up to date" requirement?

gh pr create --base main --title "fix(graph): give release_decision.rs's stale-intent sites real error causes (PR3/4)" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary

PR3 of the 4-PR `SPEC-ARCH-RELEASE-ERROR-TAXONOMY` migration (PR1: #79, PR2: #80, both merged). Based directly on `main`.

Classifies all 42 `StaleReason::legacy_unclassified()` sites in `commands/release_decision.rs` into the specific `GraphError` variant PR1 already defined for each failure family, instead of the fieldless "no release operation was authorized" message every one of them previously shared.

- **Subprocess exits/malformed output** (git rev-parse/diff-tree/show, cat-file --batch, name-status parsing, batch protocol parsing) → `ReleaseCommand{program, args, failure}` (E164), via two file-local helpers.
- **The 8 distinct merged-commit verification checks** in `derive_release_commit_decision` (the function that verifies an already-merged release commit against its committed decision file) → their own distinct `ReleaseCommitVerificationFailed{commit, reason}` (E165) variant each: `HeadMismatch`, `DecisionNotWrittenByCommit`, `NoChangesetConsumed`, `ChangelogNotTouched`, `ManifestNotInDiff`, `ManifestVersionMismatch`, `UnclaimedVersionChange`, `ClaimedPackageNotObserved` — **this is the core point of the whole migration**, since these were previously indistinguishable behind one generic message.
- Corrupt committed decision JSON → `ReleaseDecisionDecode` (E166).
- Missing changelog config on a claimed package → `ReleasePreconditionUnmet` (E170, `ChangelogConfigured`).
- Unhandled `#[non_exhaustive]` `BumpReason` arm → `UnsupportedRelease` (E168).
- Duplicate/out-of-plan `--package` selections → `ReleaseSelectionInvalid` (E169), now naming the offending package.
- Already-typed causes (`ReleasePackageId::new`, `ReleaseDecisionV1::new`, `Version::parse`) now flow through their existing `#[from]` variant instead of being discarded.
- Genuine internal invariants (plan/workspace pairing mismatch, cascade/peer via-lookup, unreachable ecosystem-format miss) → `ReleaseInvariant` (E171).

**All 42 sites classified — none left on `legacy_unclassified()`.** No new helper shared with `release.rs` (PR4, in flight independently) — kept file-local per this migration's own lesson about not stacking unmerged branches.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo clippy -p callisto-graph --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` — clean

- [x] Fixed existing tests pattern-matching the old shape; added regression tests for `HeadMismatch`, corrupt-decision-file, `ClaimedPackageNotObserved`, and duplicate/not-in-plan selection
- [x] Independently reviewed the full `derive_release_commit_decision` diff line-by-line — each of the 8 checks maps to its correct, distinct variant with unchanged logic

Confirmed — that's a real bug, not just cosmetic. Fixing it now.

**The label line**: `$INPUT_PR_LABEL` is unconditionally passed to both `compose-pr-body --label` (renders "Suggested PR Labels: `callisto: release`") *and* `gh pr create --label` / `gh pr edit --add-label` (actually applies it). It's never merely "suggested" — always applied — so the line is both redundant with GitHub's own label sidebar and factually misleading (implies an action that hasn't happened yet).

**One more real duplicate I found while checking**: in the per-package collapsible details, the `<summary>` line already shows `**pkg** \`from\` → \`to\` (severity)`, and immediately below it there's a `#### Version Change` sub-heading repeating `from ➔ to` again — same two version numbers, twice, one right after the other, inside the same expanded block.

Not duplicate, just worth naming: the executive summary table *also* shows every package's from/to/severity — but that's a top-level scan table vs. per-package expandable detail, which is a defensible UX pattern (scan once, then drill in), not the same kind of pointless repetition as the other two.

Want me to fix both (drop the "Suggested PR Labels" line entirely, and drop the redundant "Version Change" sub-heading since the summary line already carries it), or just the label one?

Rewriting a dependency's extras list or marker now goes through `Requirement::render`'s normalized form (e.g. `[a, b]` -> `[a,b]`, `; marker` -> `;marker`) rather than re-splicing the original raw substrings -- no existing test encoded the old whitespace-preserving behavior. - `callisto-manifests`'s `cargo.rs` factors `set_scalar_preserving_decor` and `set_dependency_version` out of the member-manifest (`CargoToml`) and workspace-root (`WorkspaceCargoResolver`) write paths, which independently hand-rolled the same decor-preservation dance for `[package].version` and for a dependency's bare-string/inline-table/full-table value shapes. - `callisto-graph`'s `config::resolve::load` factors `parse_package_config_fields` out of its `[[package]]` and `[[package-set]]` loops, which ran the identical release-trigger/tag-template/changelog/pre-major-inference/publish-to parsing sequence into an identical `PackageConfig` literal, differing only in the pattern-parser type and an error-message prefix. - `callisto-graph`'s `config::groups::GroupTable::validate_syntactic` and `::resolve` now loop over `[GroupKind::Fixed, GroupKind::Linked]` internally instead of writing the fixed arm and linked arm out separately. `validate_syntactic` previously had no direct unit tests; A pnpm or yarn workspace published with the wrong tool -- a live, real bug. It now detects `pnpm-lock.yaml`/`yarn.lock`/`bun.lock(b)` and builds the correct `pnpm publish --filter`/`yarn workspace ... npm publish`/`bun publish`/`npm --workspace` invocation. 250 - **cargo**: `cargo publish` ran with no `--locked` and no check that the on-disk manifest version matched the release plan. Both are restored; a mismatch now fails fast with `GraphError::OnDiskVersionDrift` instead of silently publishing a stale version. 251 - **pypi**: it built into a throwaway temp directory and uploaded whatever landed there. It now builds into `dist/` and uploads the exact `dist/-*` glob, matching the older client's intentional scoping. 252 - **git tag creation**: it inlined its own `git tag --no-sign -a ...` call with no `--` end-of-options guard against a malicious/malformed tag name. It now goes through `callisto_vcs::GitDataSource::create_tag`, which already has that guard -- extended with a new `TagSignPolicy` parameter (`RespectRepoConfig` for the existing non-durable `callisto tag` path, `ForceUnsigned` for the durable executor) so both safety properties hold together instead of one replacing the other. 253 254 The corrected argv construction and output classification for all three registry ecosystems now live in a new pure module, `callisto_graph::commands::registry_argv` (no `CommandRunner`/orchestration logic of its own). `PublishOrchestrator`, `SubprocessRegistryClient`, `AlwaysRetryPolicy`, `SystemTimeProvider`, and `parse_retry_after` are deleted: nothing in production ever constructed them (`callisto publish`'s CLI handler is an explicit dry-run-only compatibility preview; `release execute` is the only real effect path), and their retry/backoff/pre-check policy has no equivalent in the durable executor's model, which persists `Attempting` state and relies on a later re-invocation to retry rather than an in-process retry loop. 255 - What each `PublishTarget` variant means -- whether it's dispatchable, how it contributes to a package's semantic fingerprint, and whether it carries an explicit registry override -- was independently re-encoded in three separate match statements (`callisto-graph`'s `target_fingerprint`, `prepared_registry_binding`, and `publish.rs`'s per-target dispatch loop), kept in sync only by convention with `callisto-model`'s existing `PublishTarget`/`Ecosystem` capability layer. 256 257 Extended that existing layer instead of adding a second one: `PublishTarget` gains `registry_override()` (the `Npm.registry`/`Pypi.index`/`NuGet.source` payload field, unified) and `is_implemented()`. `PublishTarget` and `Ecosystem` are not 1:1 -- `GitHubRelease` is a VCS release action with no backing package `Ecosystem`, and `None` is the "not configured to publish" sentinel -- so `is_implemented()` special-cases both (`GitHubRelease` is always unimplemented, `None` is vacuously implemented) and otherwise defers to `Ecosystem::is_implemented()`. `target_fingerprint` now reuses the existing `config_str()` instead of re-hardcoding its own kind strings; `prepared_registry_binding` now calls `registry_override()` instead of its own separate match; `publish.rs`'s dispatch loop now decides its `PublishTargetNotImplemented` diagnostic via `is_implemented()` instead of independently naming `NuGet`/`GitHubRelease`. Pure refactor -- no behavior change for any existing test case. 258 - **Delete unused abstractions with zero real callers; share tag-glob compilation** 259 260 - `GitVcsProvider` trait and its `GitRepository` impl (`callisto-vcs`) -- fully superseded by the already-polymorphic `GitDataSource` trait (`GitRepository`/`ShellGit`/`GitAccess`, used generically throughout `callisto-graph`); `GitVcsProvider` had exactly one impl and zero callers anywhere in the workspace. 261 - `last_tag_for` and its `select_from_tags` helper (`callisto-graph`) -- re-exported from the crate root "for API compatibility" but the only callers were `last_tag_for`'s own unit tests; `TagIndex::build` already resolves tags via `select_from_tags_cached`. 262 - Added `callisto_vcs::compile_tag_glob` -- the one real, shared implementation of "compile a tag glob and map a compile failure to `VcsError::InvalidGlob`", now used by both `GitDataSource` backends and by `callisto-graph`'s tag matching instead of three independent copies. 263 264 No behavior change for any real caller. 265 - **Report registry-publish propagation lag with its own error, wire up missing `[lints]` tables** 266 267 `dispatch_registry`'s npm publish-succeeded-but-registry-not-yet-consistent branch used to return `GraphError::ReleaseIntentStale`, whose help text ("no release operation was authorized") is false at that call site -- an operation *was* authorized and did run; the real cause is registry propagation lag. It now returns a new `GraphError::RegistryPublishUnconfirmed { package, version }` (E157) with accurate help text. The check itself (`Ecosystem::Npm` + `PublishOutcome::Published` + registry not yet showing the version) is unchanged; only the error reported when it fires changed. Extracted the check into `require_registry_confirmation` for direct unit coverage. 268 269 `callisto-fixtures` and `callisto-moon` were missing the `[lints]` table every other crate in the workspace has, so `unsafe_code = "forbid"` and the shared clippy lint set were silently never enforced on them. `callisto-fixtures` had zero latent violations. `callisto-moon`'s `tests/moon_wasm_sandbox.rs` legitimately mutates process-wide env vars (`WARPGATE_PLUGINS_DIR`, `PATH`) under `Once`/mutex-serialized, individually SAFETY-commented `unsafe` blocks for test isolation -- `forbid` cannot be locally overridden by any in-source attribute at any nesting depth, so `callisto-moon`'s `[lints.rust]` duplicates the workspace's rust-lint table with `unsafe_code` downgraded to `"deny"` (still fails by default; a local `#[allow(unsafe_code)]` permits exactly these four reviewed sites), while `[lints.clippy]` duplicates the workspace's clippy table unchanged (Cargo's `workspace = true` inherits a `[lints]` table wholesale or not at all -- no per-tool-group partial inheritance). 270 - Replace `derive_release_commit_decision`'s 2*N per-manifest `git show` spawns with 2 batched `git cat-file --batch` invocations. 271 272 Verifying a merged release commit's claimed version roster looped over every workspace package's canonical manifests and, for each one, called `manifest_version_at` twice -- once against the parent commit, once against the release commit -- each shelling out a separate `git show :` subprocess. For a monorepo with N canonical manifests that was 2N sequential subprocess spawns to verify one release commit, on top of the `git diff-tree` call already made earlier in the same function. 273 274 Since only two distinct commits are ever queried, both are now fetched with exactly one `git cat-file --batch` invocation each: every requested manifest path is written to the child's stdin up front, and each object's blob content (or `missing`, for a manifest that didn't exist yet at the parent commit) streams back on stdout in one round trip. `CommandRunner` gains a new `run_with_stdin` method (default: `Unsupported`, so none of the many existing test-double/`moon` implementors need to change) that `CliCommandRunner` implements for real, piping input on a dedicated writer thread concurrently with draining the child's stdout/stderr so a payload larger than a pipe buffer can't deadlock. 275 276 Because this feeds release-commit trust verification, the batch-output parser is deliberately defensive rather than permissive: each response is matched against its exact requested `commit:path` object string (not a generic pattern), a declared content length that doesn't fit the remaining output or isn't followed by the protocol's separator byte fails the whole batch closed, and any leftover or truncated output once every requested path is accounted for is rejected rather than ignored. A new regression test drives `derive_release_commit_decision` with a recording `CommandRunner` double across three canonical manifests and asserts exactly 2 `cat-file --batch` invocations occur, not 6. 277 - Replace release-commit verification's changeset re-derivation with persist-and-verify. `callisto version --emit-decision ` now writes the exact release decision (package, target version, inclusion reason) it computed, alongside the manifest and changelog edits it already writes. `callisto release plan --from-release-commit` (now requiring a companion `--decision `) verifies the merged commit's actual diff against that committed decision instead of re-deriving changeset, fixed-group, linked-group, cascade, and pre-release-policy inclusion from raw git history a second time. 278 279 The prior re-derivation only understood a direct changeset-to-package match: it rejected any real release where a fixed-group cascade bumped a sibling package the deleted changeset never named, which is every release in a fixed-group workspace once more than one package versions together. Trusting the already-computed decision, tamper-checked via its own content digest, removes that entire reimplementation and the drift it was exposed to. 280 - **`GraphError::ReleaseIntentStale` (E124) becomes a struct variant carrying a real reason** 281 282 PR1 of a 4-PR migration (SPEC-ARCH-RELEASE-ERROR-TAXONOMY) fixing a confirmed architectural defect: `ReleaseIntentStale` was a fieldless unit variant constructed at ~95 sites across `commands/{release.rs,release_decision.rs,release_execution.rs}`, of which only 6 were genuine staleness -- the rest silently discarded an already-typed failure cause (a model error, a subprocess exit status, a merged-commit verification mismatch, a remote conflict, and more) behind the same generic, sometimes misleading "no release operation was authorized" message. 283 284 - `ReleaseIntentStale` is now `{ reason: StaleReason }`; its Display message appends the reason, and its diagnostic code/help text are unchanged. This is semver-breaking for any external consumer pattern-matching the old unit variant (none exist inside this workspace). 285 - `StaleReason` (`callisto-graph::commands::release`) is nameable everywhere but constructible with a real reason only from within `release.rs` itself -- `trust_evidence_changed`, `source_identity_changed`, `git_remote_changed`, and `intent_differs_from_fresh_derivation` cover the module's 6 genuine fresh-re-observation sites. Every other prior `ReleaseIntentStale` site (44 in `release.rs`, 42 in `release_decision.rs`, 2 in `release_execution.rs`) now uses a temporary, `#[deprecated]`, `pub(crate)` `StaleReason::legacy_unclassified()` migration ratchet, pinned exactly by a new architecture test and lowered to zero across PR2-PR4 as each site is given its real cause.

callisto-changelog 0.6.0 → 0.7.0 (minor) #### Version Change `0.6.0` ➔ `0.7.0` #### Release Reason ## 0.7.0 - **Parameterize six "one arm per kind" implementations on the value that varied between arms, instead of writing each arm out separately** No behavior change for any real caller in this set -- each factors an existing, independently-tested code path into a single shared implementation: - `callisto-manifests` gains `Requirement` (with `parse`/`render`), a real PEP 508 dependency-specifier type backed by a parse-render-parse idempotence property test. Rewriting a dependency's extras list or marker now goes through `Requirement::render`'s normalized form (e.g. `[a, b]` -> `[a,b]`, `; marker` -> `;marker`) rather than re-splicing the original raw substrings -- no existing test encoded the old whitespace-preserving behavior. - `callisto-manifests`'s `cargo.rs` factors `set_scalar_preserving_decor` and `set_dependency_version` out of the member-manifest (`CargoToml`) and workspace-root (`WorkspaceCargoResolver`) write paths, which independently hand-rolled the same decor-preservation dance for `[package].version` and for a dependency's bare-string/inline-table/full-table value shapes. - `callisto-graph`'s `config::resolve::load` factors `parse_package_config_fields` out of its `[[package]]` and `[[package-set]]` loops, which ran the identical release-trigger/tag-template/changelog/pre-major-inference/publish-to parsing sequence into an identical `PackageConfig` literal, differing only in the pattern-parser type and an error-message prefix. - `callisto-graph`'s `config::groups::GroupTable::validate_syntactic` and `::resolve` now loop over `[GroupKind::Fixed, GroupKind::Linked]` internally instead of writing the fixed arm and linked arm out separately. `validate_syntactic` previously had no direct unit tests; this change adds eight, covering the asymmetric cross-kind member-conflict check the single shared implementation had to reproduce exactly. - `callisto-changelog`'s `write::prepend` now computes `rest` once across its three header-shape branches (blank line after the H1, no blank line, no matching H1 at all) and runs the shared five-statement splice a single time, instead of each branch repeating the same splice after computing its own `rest`. - `callisto-moon`'s `locator.rs` factors a single `detect_single_ecosystem` helper for `declared_edges`'s from/to ecosystem lookup (previously two copies of the same if/else-if chain), and routes both `projects()`'s multi-ecosystem enumeration and `declared_edges`'s single-ecosystem lookup through `Ecosystem::CANONICAL` instead of separately hardcoded manifest-filename checks. - Released together with the `workspace` fixed group.
callisto-cli 0.6.0 → 0.7.0 (minor) #### Version Change `0.6.0` ➔ `0.7.0` #### Release Reason ## 0.7.0 - **Fix three error/diagnostic messages that told the operator the wrong cause** - `callisto-vcs`: `ReleaseWorkspaceLock::acquire` reported every lock-acquisition failure -- permission denied, disk full, a filesystem that doesn't support `flock`, or any other I/O error -- as "another Callisto release already holds this workspace lock". It now distinguishes true contention (matched against `fs2::lock_contended_error()`'s `ErrorKind`, the same signal `fs2` itself uses) from other I/O failures, and reports the real underlying cause for the latter instead of misattributing it to a held lock. - `callisto-graph`: `IdentityResolver::resolve` collapsed both an unsupported-ecosystem case and a genuine `PackageId` parse failure into `GraphError::AmbiguousName`, which is semantically wrong for both (neither is a name-ambiguity problem) and discarded the real reason. Two new variants -- `UnsupportedIdentityEcosystem` and `PackageIdentifierParse` (carrying the underlying `PackageIdParseError`) -- now report each failure's own accurate cause. - `callisto-cli`: `callisto add --package name:severity` rejected an invalid severity with "Must be patch, minor, or major.", omitting `none`, which `Severity::from_str` has always accepted. The message (and the `--package` flag's help text) now lists all four accepted values. - **Delete unused abstractions with zero real callers** Removed as pure dead-code deletions -- each had exactly one implementation (or none) reachable only through its own tests, with every real call site already going through the underlying concrete type or free function directly: - `PackageIdentityResolver` trait (`callisto-model`) -- a one-line delegate to `PackageId::matches`. - `ChangesetStorage` trait (`callisto-model`, re-exported from `callisto-manifests`) -- a one-line method-call spelling of the free function `atomic_write`. - `ManifestCstEditor` trait and its blanket impl (`callisto-manifests`) -- combined mutate-and-persist in one call, which no real caller used and which would have been the wrong shape anyway: `apply.rs` deliberately calls `write_version`/`update_dependency_spec` and `persist` as separate steps to batch several writes before one flush. - `ReleaseEffectAdapter` trait and `PreparedReleaseEffectAdapter` (`callisto-graph`) -- `execute_release`/`execute_release_with_artifacts` now call the prepared capability's dispatch directly instead of going through a single-implementation generic seam. - `RawMoonYml`/`RawMoonExtensions`/`RawMoonCallistoConfig` (`callisto-graph`) -- a config schema nothing in this crate ever deserialized a `moon.yml` file into. - `ReportPresenter` trait (`callisto-cli`) -- only implemented by a test-only fake built solely to exercise the trait's own default method. - `--skip-publish-precheck` CLI flag and `check_credentials` (`callisto-cli`) -- the flag was parsed and immediately discarded; `check_credentials` is `#[cfg(test)]`-gated and was never compiled into the production binary. No behavior change for any real caller. - Four instances of a value being re-derived instead of reused, all fixed the same way (compute once, have both branches consume the same value): - `crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/status.rs`'s `--check` exit code recomputed `has_changesets` from `report.packages` instead of reading the field `callisto-graph`'s status command already computed and stored on `StatusReport`. - `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/validate.rs`'s `--staged` and `--since` branches each ran their own `git diff`, error-mapped it, and filtered changesets identically, differing only in the git args. Factored into one `changesets_touched_by` helper. - `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/tag.rs`'s floating-major tag computation (template lookup, version extract, grammar resolve, parse, render, existence check) was written out fully in both the dry-run preview branch and the write branch. Factored into `plan_floating_major`, called by both; the permit still gates only the actual `create_floating_major` call. - `crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/publish.rs` and `plan_publish.rs` independently wired up the identical `load_workspace` -> `plan_publish` pipeline. Factored into a shared `plan_publish::build_plan` both commands call. - Two `callisto-cli` sites re-derived `PublishPlan` emptiness by hand instead of calling the canonical `PublishPlan::is_empty()` (`callisto-model`), which already ANDs all five plan fields specifically to avoid a hand-listed check silently missing one (e.g. `pypi_packages`): - `commands/publish.rs`'s `write_dry_run_text` hand-listed all five fields with `&&`. - `render/mod.rs`'s `render_publish` computed a `total_packages` sum of the four package-field lengths plus a separate `releases.is_empty()` check. Both now call `plan.is_empty()`. No behavior change -- `render_publish` keeps `total_packages` for its package-section-skip branch and package counts, only the true-emptiness branch now calls `is_empty()`. - Replace `derive_release_commit_decision`'s 2*N per-manifest `git show` spawns with 2 batched `git cat-file --batch` invocations. Verifying a merged release commit's claimed version roster looped over every workspace package's canonical manifests and, for each one, called `manifest_version_at` twice -- once against the parent commit, once against the release commit -- each shelling out a separate `git show :` subprocess. For a monorepo with N canonical manifests that was 2N sequential subprocess spawns to verify one release commit, on top of the `git diff-tree` call already made earlier in the same function. Since only two distinct commits are ever queried, both are now fetched with exactly one `git cat-file --batch` invocation each: every requested manifest path is written to the child's stdin up front, and each object's blob content (or `missing`, for a manifest that didn't exist yet at the parent commit) streams back on stdout in one round trip. `CommandRunner` gains a new `run_with_stdin` method (default: `Unsupported`, so none of the many existing test-double/`moon` implementors need to change) that `CliCommandRunner` implements for real, piping input on a dedicated writer thread concurrently with draining the child's stdout/stderr so a payload larger than a pipe buffer can't deadlock. Because this feeds release-commit trust verification, the batch-output parser is deliberately defensive rather than permissive: each response is matched against its exact requested `commit:path` object string (not a generic pattern), a declared content length that doesn't fit the remaining output or isn't followed by the protocol's separator byte fails the whole batch closed, and any leftover or truncated output once every requested path is accounted for is rejected rather than ignored. A new regression test drives `derive_release_commit_decision` with a recording `CommandRunner` double across three canonical manifests and asserts exactly 2 `cat-file --batch` invocations occur, not 6. - Replace release-commit verification's changeset re-derivation with persist-and-verify. `callisto version --emit-decision ` now writes the exact release decision (package, target version, inclusion reason) it computed, alongside the manifest and changelog edits it already writes. `callisto release plan --from-release-commit` (now requiring a companion `--decision `) verifies the merged commit's actual diff against that committed decision instead of re-deriving changeset, fixed-group, linked-group, cascade, and pre-release-policy inclusion from raw git history a second time. The prior re-derivation only understood a direct changeset-to-package match: it rejected any real release where a fixed-group cascade bumped a sibling package the deleted changeset never named, which is every release in a fixed-group workspace once more than one package versions together. Trusting the already-computed decision, tamper-checked via its own content digest, removes that entire reimplementation and the drift it was exposed to. - `snapshot` and `tag` now share a new `abort_on_crosscheck_failures` helper (`crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/mod.rs`) instead of each hand-rolling an identical ~15-line block that cloned `ws.graph.diagnostics()`, called `callisto_graph::commands::escalate`, filtered for `Error` severity, and formatted the same abort message. **Fix**: that duplicated block called `escalate(&mut diags, true, true)` -- hardcoding both the `strict` and `strict_graph` arguments to `true` -- instead of passing through the command's actual flags, the way `status`, `validate`, and `version` already do via their `*Options` structs. In practice this meant `--strict-graph` had no CLI flag at all on `snapshot`/`tag` and no way to take effect on its own: the escalation block only ran from behind an `if args.strict` gate, so a workspace-graph-only strict check silently did nothing unless `--strict` was also passed. Both commands now accept a real `--strict-graph` flag (`SnapshotArgs`/`TagArgs` gained a `strict_graph: bool` field) and pass `args.strict`/`args.strict_graph` through to `escalate` unconditionally, matching the sibling commands' semantics: `--strict` still escalates graph diagnostics too (per `escalate`'s own `strict || strict_graph` rule), and `--strict-graph` alone now escalates them as well. - **Parse GitHub repository and Git tag identity instead of validating ad hoc (audit pattern F)** `callisto-model` gains two real identity types replacing several independent, inconsistent ad hoc validations of the same concepts: - `GitHubRepository::parse` replaces three separate `owner/repo` checks: `GitHubAttestationPolicyV1`'s `is_safe_github_repository` (a bare `split_once('/')` with no character-class check at all), `release_pr.rs`'s `validate_repository`/`valid_repo_part` (ASCII alphanumeric plus `-_.` per part), and an entirely unvalidated `format!("{owner}/{repository}")` built from a parsed Git remote URL in `callisto-graph`. Every caller now parses through one charset rule: both `owner` and `repo` must be non-empty, ASCII alphanumeric plus `-`, `_`, `.`, and must not start or end with `-`. `GitHubAttestationPolicyV1::repository`, `GitHubArtifactAttestationV1::repository`, `ArtifactSlotId::new`'s `repository` parameter, `ReleasePrConfigV1::repository`, `ReleasePrSnapshotV2::repository`, and `ReleasePrPullRequestV2::head_repository` all change from `String` to `GitHubRepository`; it serializes and deserializes as its plain `"owner/repo"` string form (matching `ReleasePackageId`'s existing convention), so no wire-format change. **Behavior change**: this is a real tightening at a security-sensitive validation boundary (`GitHubAttestationPolicyV1` gates the `gh attestation verify --repo ` provenance check), not just an internal refactor. A value that previously passed `is_safe_github_repository` can now be rejected -- concretely, embedded whitespace (for example `"owner name/repo"`), a leading or trailing `-` in either part, or more than one `/`. - **Render the `governed by = (default)` attribution line for bumps and diagnostics (§13 invariant 28)** `render::attribution::attribution_line` has existed since the config-provenance work landed but had zero callers: `render_version`'s text output printed a bump's package/from/to and a diagnostic's severity/message, but never consulted `BumpRecord.governed_by` / `Diagnostic.governed_by` at all, so an operator running `callisto version` (or `--format text` generally) had no way to see which `callisto.toml` key was responsible for a bump or warning, or whether that key was set explicitly or left at its default. `render_version` now takes the workspace's `&ResolvedConfig` and prints the attribution line under any bump or diagnostic whose `governed_by` is `Some`, via the same `attribution_line` the spec always intended to render it (`callisto-graph` computes the key, `callisto-cli` looks up and renders its current value and provenance -- neither crate re-derives the other's half). `render_diagnostics` gained a matching `Option<&ResolvedConfig>` parameter so it can do the same for any report's diagnostics; every caller other than `render_version` passes `None` today, since no other report ever populates `governed_by` on a `Diagnostic` yet, so their output is unchanged. **Signature change**: `render::render_version(report, w)` is now `render::render_version(report, cfg, w)`. `render::render_diagnostics(diagnostics, w)` is now `render::render_diagnostics(diagnostics, cfg, w)`. content.text:
## Diagnosis

I pulled the actual live release PR (#55) as a real example: **629 lines** for a 10-package release. Four causes, in order of impact:

1. **Verbatim duplication across grouped packages.** 6 of the 10 packages share a "workspace" fixed group, and each gets its *own* full `<details>` block with the **entire changelog dump repeated identically**. This is the dominant source of bloat — the same ~15 bullet points, word-for-word, six times.
2. **Everything defaults open.** Any minor-or-major bump auto-expands its block. Since most real releases are minor/major (patch-only releases are the exception), this means nothing actually collapses — the whole wall of text renders immediately with zero clicks.
3. **Version info shown three times per package**: once in the summary table row, again in the collapsible `<summary>` line, again under a "#### Version Change" sub-heading right below it.
4. **"Suggested PR Labels" line** — duplicates GitHub's own label sidebar, and is factually wrong since the label isn't "suggested," it's always actually applied (confirmed: the shell script passes it to `gh pr create --label` / `gh pr edit --add-label` unconditionally).

## Proposal, in order of impact

1. **Dedup identical release-reason content.** Group bumps by their exact rendered changelog text (not by declared group name — content-equality is what's actually visible as duplication, and stays robust even if grouping metadata doesn't perfectly align). Render **one** `<details>` block per unique content, with a summary naming every package it covers, instead of one full block per package. This alone would cut PR #55's body roughly in half.
2. **Change the auto-open rule**: open only if the block contains a **major** bump. Minor/patch content stays collapsed — the summary table already shows every package's severity and target version, so nothing is hidden, just not force-expanded.
3. **Drop the "#### Version Change" sub-heading** — repeats the line directly above it.
4. **Drop "Suggested PR Labels" entirely**, and remove the now-pointless `--label` flag on `compose-pr-body` (its only consumer) plus the corresponding pass-through in the action script.

## Scope
- `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/pr_body.rs` (the actual redesign)
- `crates/callisto-cli/src/cli.rs` + `commands/compose_pr_body.rs` (drop dead `--label` flag)
- `.github/actions/callisto-action/scripts/create-or-update-release-pr.sh` (stop passing `--label` to `compose-pr-body`; keep it on the real `gh pr create`/`edit` calls)
- Existing tests updated, insta snapshot regenerated, new tests for the dedup grouping and open/closed rule

## Two design calls I want your read on before I build this

**Grouping key** — dedup by exact rendered content (automatic, robust, but "invisible" logic), or by the `BumpReason`'s declared group name (fixed/linked group — more semantically labeled, but needs a fallback for packages that share text without sharing a declared group)?

**Open/closed rule** — "open only if it contains a major bump," or would you rather something else (always closed by default, or open just the first block)?

content.text:
A few worth adding, a few worth skipping — here's what I'd actually use:

**Worth using:**

1. **Match the alert type to severity.** GitHub supports 5 alert types: `NOTE`, `TIP`, `IMPORTANT`, `WARNING`, `CAUTION`. Currently the code only uses `NOTE` and `IMPORTANT` for major bumps — `WARNING` fits a breaking change better semantically ("risk," not just "key info").

2. **One outer collapsible wrapping the whole "What's Changing" section**, closed by default unless a major bump exists anywhere. This is the single biggest lever left for "dense and hard to follow": a routine minor/patch release would render as just the title blurb, the summary table, one `[!NOTE]`, and a single closed toggle — *"▶ What's Changing (8 changes across 10 packages)"*. Nothing else renders until you click. A release with a major bump auto-opens it, since that's the case where you want the detail visible immediately.

3. **Severity emoji in the summary table** (🔴 major / 🟡 minor / 🟢 patch) alongside the existing text — free scannability, no new dependency.

**Worth skipping, and why:**

- **Badges (shields.io-style)** — pulls in external images for a cosmetic gain; adds a fragile network dependency to something that should render identically offline/rate-limited.
- **Mermaid diagrams** for cascade chains — there's no real graph to draw here beyond what "Cascade from `X`" already says in one line; would be novelty for its own sake.
- **Footnotes** — they relocate long text, they don't hide it. `<details>` already does the actual job (collapsed by default), so footnotes would be a strictly weaker version of what we're already doing.
- **Anchor/jump-links at the top** — only worth it if the body is *still* long after the restructure. Premature before we've measured that.

So the combined shape: table → note/warning → one collapsed (or auto-opened-if-major) "What's Changing" wrapper → per-change collapsibles inside it → instructions footer, same as before.

content.text:
No — I'd leave the changeset file format and the per-package `CHANGELOG.md` output alone. Here's why, confirmed from the actual code:

`Changeset { entries: Vec<Entry>, summary: String }` — one shared summary, fanned out verbatim to every listed package. That's the standard model (matches the JS `@changesets/changesets` convention this whole system is modeled on), and it's *correct* for `CHANGELOG.md`: each package's own changelog needs to be self-contained and readable in isolation — someone looking at just `callisto-model`'s changelog shouldn't have to cross-reference `callisto-graph`'s to understand why a version bumped. Repetition across separate files, read separately, at separate times, isn't a real cost.

The duplication that's actually a problem — the one from PR #55 — only exists in the **PR body**, because that's the one place all N packages' fanned-out copies of the same changeset end up rendered into a single document, read in one sitting. That's an artifact of `pr_body.rs`'s rendering choice (loop per package, render each package's full section), not of the changeset format or the changelog writer. So the fix stays exactly where we already scoped it — group the PR body by change instead of by package — with zero changes to changeset parsing, authoring, or `CHANGELOG.md` output.

One adjacent idea I'd flag but *not* build unless it becomes a real pain point: today a changeset's summary text is identical for a package that was the actual site of the change versus one just riding along in a fixed group with no direct code change of its own. If that ever confuses someone reading a bystander package's changelog, the fix would be a small optional field on `Entry` (e.g. `role: Direct | Cascaded`) so a bystander's entry could say "bumped via workspace fixed group" instead of repeating the unrelated summary.
