#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Executes a typed Callisto release-PR decision. Forge reads stay here; all
# create/update policy belongs to `callisto release-pr decide`.
#
# The managed branch is never pushed with the Git wire protocol: on a public
# repository, GITHUB_TOKEN cannot write `.github/workflows/*` that way, nor
# through createCommitOnBranch's own fileChanges, on any ref (confirmed
# directly against this repository). Instead, the generated
# version-bump changes are committed via the forge commit API onto a
# deterministic staging branch rooted at the current base commit -- which
# never needs to touch `.github/workflows/*`, since that path is inherited
# unchanged from the base -- and only then is the managed branch's ref moved
# onto that commit. A ref move is not itself a write to that path.
set -euo pipefail

cd "$INPUT_CWD"

# This checkout starts on the configured base. Preserve its exact commit for
# both observations; the working tree changes below (git add -A) never
# create a local commit -- the real commit is made remotely, via the forge
# commit API, on the staging branch.
base_commit=$(git rev-parse HEAD)

release_pr_snapshot() {
  local raw_prs
  raw_prs=$(gh pr list --state open --base "$INPUT_BRANCH" --limit 1000 --json number,headRefName,headRepository,headRefOid)
  jq -cn \
    --arg repository "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
    --arg base_branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" \
    --arg base_commit "$base_commit" \
    --argjson raw_prs "$raw_prs" \
    '{
      schemaVersion: 2,
      repository: $repository,
      baseBranch: $base_branch,
      baseCommit: $base_commit,
      openPullRequests: [$raw_prs[] | {
        number,
        headRepository: (.headRepository.nameWithOwner // ""),
        headBranch: .headRefName,
        headCommit: .headRefOid
      }]
    }'
}

snapshot=$(release_pr_snapshot)
decision=$(callisto --format json release-pr decide \
  --snapshot "$snapshot" \
  --repository "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
  --base-branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" \
  --release-branch "$INPUT_RELEASE_BRANCH")
decision_kind=$(jq -r '.action.kind' <<< "$decision")

case "$decision_kind" in
  noop)
    echo 'hasChangesets=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    matrix=$(callisto matrix --format json | jq -c '[.platformTargets[].targets[]] | unique_by(.artifactName)')
    echo "nativeMatrix=$matrix" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo '::notice::No changesets. This action does not publish, tag, download artifacts, or create releases; use the durable repository workflow.'
    exit 0
    ;;
  create)
    release_branch=$(jq -r '.action.branch' <<< "$decision")
    staging_branch=$(jq -r '.action.stagingBranch' <<< "$decision")
    existing_pr=''
    ;;
  update)
    existing_pr=$(jq -r '.action.pullRequestNumber' <<< "$decision")
    release_branch=$(jq -r '.action.branch' <<< "$decision")
    staging_branch=$(jq -r '.action.stagingBranch' <<< "$decision")
    ;;
  *) echo "::error::Callisto returned unsupported release PR decision kind: $decision_kind"; exit 1 ;;
esac

echo 'hasChangesets=true' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
if [[ -n "$existing_pr" ]]; then
  existing_body=$(gh pr view "$existing_pr" --json body --jq '.body')
  body=$(printf '%s' "$existing_body" | callisto compose-pr-body --existing-body - --label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" --branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" --format text)
else
  body=$(callisto compose-pr-body --label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" --branch "$INPUT_BRANCH" --format text)
fi

read -ra command <<< "$INPUT_VERSION_COMMAND"
command+=(--emit-decision "$INPUT_DECISION_PATH")
"${command[@]}"
git add -A
test -n "$(git status --porcelain)" || { echo '::error::pending changesets produced no release-PR delta'; exit 1; }

plan_file=$(mktemp)
callisto --format json release-pr commit-plan --base-commit "$base_commit" --message "$INPUT_COMMIT_MESSAGE" --out "$plan_file"
local_tree=$(git write-tree)

staging_created=false
cleanup_staging() {
  if [[ "$staging_created" == true ]]; then
    gh api -X DELETE "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs/heads/$staging_branch" > /dev/null 2>&1 \
      || echo "::warning::could not delete staging branch $staging_branch; the next run reclaims this deterministic name"
  fi
  rm -f "$plan_file" body.json
}
trap cleanup_staging EXIT

# A local diff does not authorize a stale forge write. Re-observe immediately
# before mutating the remote branch, then again before moving the managed
# ref, then again before GitHub label/PR writes.
callisto release-pr verify --decision "$decision" --snapshot "$(release_pr_snapshot)" > /dev/null

if gh api -X PATCH "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs/heads/$staging_branch" -f sha="$base_commit" -F force=true > /dev/null 2>&1; then
  :
else
  gh api -X POST "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs" -f ref="refs/heads/$staging_branch" -f sha="$base_commit" > /dev/null
fi
staging_created=true

jq -n \
  --arg repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
  --arg branch "$staging_branch" \
  --arg headline "$INPUT_COMMIT_MESSAGE" \
  --slurpfile plan "$plan_file" \
  '{
    query: "mutation($input: CreateCommitOnBranchInput!) { createCommitOnBranch(input: $input) { commit { oid } } }",
    variables: {
      input: {
        branch: {repositoryNameWithOwner: $repo, branchName: $branch},
        message: {headline: $headline},
        expectedHeadOid: $plan[0].baseCommit,
        fileChanges: {
          additions: [$plan[0].additions[] | {path, contents: .contentsBase64}],
          deletions: $plan[0].deletions
        }
      }
    }
  }' > body.json

new_sha=$(gh api graphql --input body.json --jq '.data.createCommitOnBranch.commit.oid')
remote_tree=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/commits/$new_sha" --jq '.tree.sha')
if [[ "$remote_tree" != "$local_tree" ]]; then
  echo "::error::forge commit tree $remote_tree does not match the locally staged tree $local_tree; refusing to move $release_branch"
  exit 1
fi

callisto release-pr verify --decision "$decision" --snapshot "$(release_pr_snapshot)" > /dev/null

if [[ "$decision_kind" == update ]]; then
  gh api -X PATCH "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs/heads/$release_branch" -f sha="$new_sha" -F force=true > /dev/null
else
  if ! gh api -X POST "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs" -f ref="refs/heads/$release_branch" -f sha="$new_sha" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
    gh api -X PATCH "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs/heads/$release_branch" -f sha="$new_sha" -F force=true > /dev/null
  fi
fi
moved_sha=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/refs/heads/$release_branch" --jq '.object.sha')
if [[ "$moved_sha" != "$new_sha" ]]; then
  echo "::error::$release_branch points at $moved_sha after the update, expected $new_sha; a concurrent write may have raced this run"
  exit 1
fi

callisto release-pr verify --decision "$decision" --snapshot "$(release_pr_snapshot)" > /dev/null

label_exists=$(gh label list --limit 1000 --json name --jq 'any(.[]; .name == env.INPUT_PR_LABEL)')
if [[ "$label_exists" != true ]]; then
  gh label create "$INPUT_PR_LABEL" --color 0e8a16 --description 'Callisto release packages'
fi

case "$decision_kind" in
  create)
    gh pr create --head "$release_branch" --base "$INPUT_BRANCH" --title "$INPUT_TITLE" --body "$body" --label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL"
    ;;
  update)
    gh pr edit "$existing_pr" --title "$INPUT_TITLE" --body "$body" --add-label "$INPUT_PR_LABEL"
    ;;
esac

---
callisto-graph: minor
callisto-cli: minor
---

**Restructure the release PR body to group by change instead of by package, and drop redundant/misleading sections**

A single `.changeset/*.md` file can name several packages, and its summary was copied verbatim into every one of them (correct and desirable for each package's own standalone `CHANGELOG.md`) -- but the PR body then rendered that same text once per package it touched, producing bodies with the same paragraphs repeated multiple times for any release spanning a fixed/linked group or a multi-package changeset. A real 10-package release PR measured at 629 lines.

- `compose-pr-body`'s `### 📦 What's Changing` section (renamed from `Package Release Details`) now groups by the underlying change (a changeset file, a commit, a dependency/peer bump) and lists every package it affects in one block, instead of one full block per package. A package bumped only via a fixed/linked group with no direct change of its own is now named in a short note instead of getting an empty-looking collapsible.
- The whole section is wrapped in one collapsible, closed by default and open only when the release contains a major bump; each change's own block follows the same rule. A routine minor/patch release now renders as just the summary table, one note, and a single closed toggle.
- The redundant "#### Version Change" sub-heading is gone (already shown one line above in each block's `<summary>`), and the major-bump callout uses `[!WARNING]` instead of `[!IMPORTANT]`.
- The summary table's Bump column now includes a severity emoji (🔴/🟡/🟢) for at-a-glance scanning.
- The "Suggested PR Labels" line is removed: the label it named was never merely suggested (the release-PR script always applies it via `gh pr create --label`/`gh pr edit --add-label`), so the line was both redundant with GitHub's own label UI and factually misleading. `compose-pr-body`'s now-pointless `--label` flag is removed along with it (`ComposePrBodyArgs`/`PrBodyOptions` drop the `labels` field); the release-PR action script no longer passes `--label` to `compose-pr-body`, only to the real `gh pr create`/`gh pr edit` calls where it's actually applied.

No changes to changeset authoring, parsing, or per-package `CHANGELOG.md` output -- this is scoped entirely to the PR body, the one place the same fanned-out content is read together in a single sitting.

## Summary

Restructures the auto-generated release PR body to fix real density problems, measured against the actual live PR #55 (629 lines for a 10-package release).

**Root cause**: a single `.changeset/*.md` file can name several packages, and its summary is copied verbatim into every one of them (correct and desirable for each package's own standalone `CHANGELOG.md`) — but the PR body rendered that same text once per package it touched. A changeset naming 4 packages showed its full text 4 times in one document read in one sitting.

## What changed

- **Group by change, not by package.** `### 📦 What's Changing` (renamed from `Package Release Details`) now groups entries by their underlying identity (a changeset filename, a commit, a dependency/peer bump) and lists every affected package in one block, instead of repeating the same content once per package. Verified end-to-end with the real binary: two packages sharing one changeset now render it exactly once, with both packages named in the block's `<summary>`.
- **Bystander packages get a note, not an empty block.** A package bumped only because it shares a fixed/linked group — no direct change of its own — is named in a one-line note instead of getting its own collapsible with nothing substantive inside.
- **Two-level collapsing.** The whole "What's Changing" section is one outer collapsible, closed by default and open only when the release contains a major bump; each change's own inner block follows the same rule. A routine minor/patch release now renders as just the summary table, one `[!NOTE]`, and a single closed toggle — nothing else renders until clicked.
- **Drop redundant/misleading content**: the "#### Version Change" sub-heading (already shown one line above in the `<summary>`) and the "Suggested PR Labels" line (the label was never merely suggested — the release-PR script always applies it via `gh pr create --label`/`gh pr edit --add-label` — so the line duplicated GitHub's own label UI while being factually wrong). Removed the now-pointless `--label` flag on `compose-pr-body` along with it.
- **Small polish**: `[!WARNING]` instead of `[!IMPORTANT]` for the major-bump callout; a severity emoji (🔴/🟡/🟢) in the summary table's Bump column.

**Out of scope, deliberately**: changeset authoring/parsing and per-package `CHANGELOG.md` output are untouched. ---
callisto-graph: patch
---

**Stop hiding the release PR's change list behind an extra collapsible**

The outer `<details>` wrapper added around `### 📦 What's Changing` (closed by default unless a major bump is present) made the entire list of what changed invisible until clicked — including for a routine minor-only release, where a reviewer had to open the wrapper just to see the *names* of the changes before deciding whether to read any of them.

The outer wrapper is removed; the list of changes (each one's own `<summary>` naming the change and the packages it affects) is now always directly visible, replaced only by a plain `**N change(s) across M package(s):**` count line. Each individual change's own body still collapses by default and opens automatically when it contains a major bump — only the actual prose text collapses, never the fact that a change exists.

message.content: Think critically about what the point of a release PR is, what should we be hiding, if anything??

lastPrompt: Think critically about what the point of a release PR is, what should we be hiding, if anything??

content.text:
The release PR isn't a code-review artifact — the code was already reviewed in the PRs that authored each changeset. This PR's actual job is to gate a **publish action**: merging triggers real releases to crates.io/npm/PyPI. So the real question a merger is answering is narrower than "read everything": *"am I comfortable shipping this exact set of version bumps right now?"* That decomposes into two things, and only two:

1. **Do the bumps look right** — right packages, right severities, nothing surprising.
2. **Is anything breaking** — and if so, does it deserve a closer look before I press publish.

Given that framing:

- **Never hide**: the version table (severity, package, target) and anything touching a **major** bump. That's the actual decision-relevant content, and it's already how the current design behaves (majors auto-open, table always visible).
- **Fine to hide, but never disappear**: the full prose of minor/patch changes. Their content was already approved once, in the PR that wrote the changeset — the release-PR reviewer isn't re-reviewing that work, just confirming the aggregate is safe to ship. So the *existence* of each change and *which packages it affects* has to stay visible (that's the current, correct behavior after #84), but the paragraph of prose inside is legitimately low-value to force in front of every reviewer, every time.

One gap this reasoning surfaces that we haven't addressed: **ordering.** Right now packages render in plan order (roughly topological/alphabetical), so a major bump could be row 8 of 10 in the table — a merger has to scan the whole thing to confirm nothing's breaking. If the real question is "is anything breaking," majors should be unmissable, not just auto-opened wherever they happen to fall. I'd sort the table (and the change list) so majors lead, not trailing wherever their package name happens to sort.

I wouldn't go further than that (e.g., collapsing the table itself, or summarizing patch-only rows into one line) — the table is the audit trail of exact versions, and compressing it trades away the "is this exactly what I expect" scan the merger actually needs. Want me to add the major-first ordering?

---
callisto-graph: patch
---

**Order the release PR's summary table and change list by severity, major first**

A reviewer merging a release PR is really answering one question: is anything breaking? Before this change, both the summary table and the "What's Changing" list rendered in plan order (roughly topological/declaration order), so a major bump could land anywhere among a dozen rows — a reviewer had to scan the whole table to be sure nothing was breaking, even though a major bump's own detail block already auto-opens.

Both the table and the change list are now sorted by severity descending (major, then minor, then patch/none), stable within each tier so otherwise-equal rows keep their original relative order. A breaking change is now always the first thing visible, in both places, regardless of where its package name or declaration would otherwise have put it.

content.text: Added onto **PR #84**: both the summary table and the change list now sort major-first (stable within each severity tier), so a breaking change is always the first thing visible regardless of declaration order. === workflow lines 100-150 ===
    name: Identify a merged Callisto release PR
    needs: [verify, version-pr]
    if: needs.version-pr.outputs.has_pending_changesets == 'false'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      is_release_pr: ${{ steps.candidate.outputs.is_release_pr }}
    steps:
      - id: candidate
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # This only schedules the job. `release plan` verifies the actual
          # parent-to-merge delta; labels and PR metadata are never authority.
          # The GitHub API check is complementary provenance evidence: a
          # trusted merge must be both an actual merge of the managed PR and
          # a GitHub-verified signed commit. It cannot be a direct push.
          prs=$(gh api --paginate "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${GITHUB_SHA}/pulls" --jq '[.[] | select(.merged_at != null and .base.ref == "main" and (.head.ref == "callisto/version-packages" or (.head.ref | test("^callisto/version-packages--[0-9a-f]{40}$"))))] | length')
          verified=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${GITHUB_SHA}" --jq '.commit.verification.verified')
          if [[ "$prs" == 1 && "$verified" == true ]]; then
            echo 'is_release_pr=true' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo 'is_release_pr=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  plan:
    name: Derive ephemeral intent from the merged release commit
    needs: release-candidate
    if: needs.release-candidate.outputs.is_release_pr == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - name: Derive and hash intent
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          callisto release plan --from-release-commit "$GITHUB_SHA" --decision .callisto/release-decision.json --out release-intent.json
          shasum -a 256 release-intent.json > release-intent.json.sha256
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: |
            release-intent.json
            release-intent.json.sha256

content.text: Found the root cause. At the release commit, `callisto version` bumped every crate's `version` field in each `Cargo.toml` from `0.6.0` → `0.7.0`, but the committed `Cargo.lock` still lists those workspace members at their old `0.6.0` version. A plain `cargo build` on a fresh checkout notices the mismatch and silently rewrites `Cargo.lock` — which dirties the worktree and trips the "release trust requires a clean worktree" check (E051) downstream. This is a version-bump bug, not anything from PR #83/#84. Let's find where Cargo.lock is (or isn't) updated during the version-bump.

name: 'Callisto Release-PR Action'
description: 'Creates or updates a Callisto release PR; durable execution belongs to the repository workflow'
inputs:
  version_command:
    description: 'Version command; defaults to callisto version. `--emit-decision <decision_path>` is always appended, so a replacement command must also accept it (typically by wrapping `callisto version` itself).'
    required: false
    default: 'callisto version'
  decision_path:
    description: 'Path, relative to cwd, where the version command records the exact release decision this PR carries. Committed alongside the manifest and changelog edits; `callisto release plan --from-release-commit` verifies the merged commit against this file rather than re-deriving release policy.'
    required: false
    default: '.callisto/release-decision.json'
  commit_message:
    description: 'Release-PR commit message'
    required: false
    default: 'chore(release): version packages'
  title:
    description: 'Release-PR title'
    required: false
    default: 'chore(release): version packages'
  pr_label:
    description: 'Release-PR label'
    required: false
    default: 'callisto: release'
  setup_git_user:
    description: 'Unused no-op, kept for backward compatibility. The managed branch is committed through the forge commit API, not a local `git commit`, so no Git identity is ever configured.'
    required: false
    default: 'true'
  branch:
    description: 'Base branch for the release PR'
    required: false
    default: 'main'
  release_branch:
    description: 'Branch managed for the release PR'
    required: false
    default: 'callisto/version-packages'
  github_token:
    description: 'Optional GitHub token for pull-request and forge commit API operations. The managed branch is never pushed with `git push`; the default GITHUB_TOKEN is sufficient even on a public repository, since the executor never writes `.github/workflows/*`.'
    required: false
    default: ''
  setup_callisto:
    description: 'Install the Callisto environment before running'
    required: false
    default: 'true'
  cwd:
    description: 'Workspace directory'
    required: false
    default: '.'
outputs:
  hasChangesets:
    description: 'Whether pending changesets were found'
    value: ${{ steps.version-pr.outputs.hasChangesets }}
  published:
    description: 'Always false: this action never publishes'
    value: 'false'
  publishedPackages:
    description: 'Always an empty JSON array'
    value: '[]'
  nativeMatrix:
    description: 'Native build matrix preview'
    value: ${{ steps.version-pr.outputs.nativeMatrix }}
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - name: Setup Callisto Environment
      if: inputs.setup_callisto == 'true'
      uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
    - name: Create or update release PR
      id: version-pr
      shell: bash
      env:
        INPUT_VERSION_COMMAND: ${{ inputs.version_command }}
        INPUT_DECISION_PATH: ${{ inputs.decision_path }}
        INPUT_COMMIT_MESSAGE: ${{ inputs.commit_message }}
        INPUT_TITLE: ${{ inputs.title }}
        INPUT_PR_LABEL: ${{ inputs.pr_label }}
        INPUT_SETUP_GIT_USER: ${{ inputs.setup_git_user }}
        INPUT_BRANCH: ${{ inputs.branch }}
        INPUT_RELEASE_BRANCH: ${{ inputs.release_branch }}
        INPUT_CWD: ${{ inputs.cwd }}

        # inherited environment variable. Using the context also works for the

name: Release

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: release-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  verify:
    name: Verify release candidate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Build local Callisto
        uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local

      - name: Install just
        uses: extractions/setup-just@53165ef7e734c5c07cb06b3c8e7b647c5aa16db3 # v4.0.0
        with:
          just-version: '1.58.0'

      - name: Format Check
        run: just fmt-check

      - name: Clippy Lints
        run: just lint

      - name: Install release verification tools
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@e67fa11c4b9316fa714ddf0abed07a0c3143b95b # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-nextest,ripgrep

      - name: Unit & Integration Tests
        run: just test

      - name: WASM Target Check
        run: just wasm-check

      - name: Install cargo-deny
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@e67fa11c4b9316fa714ddf0abed07a0c3143b95b # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-deny

      - name: Supply Chain Audit
        run: just audit

      - name: Reject mutable GitHub Actions references
        run: .github/tests/verify-action-pins.sh

  version-pr:
    name: Create or update the Callisto release PR
    needs: verify
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
    outputs:
      has_pending_changesets: ${{ steps.version-pr.outputs.hasChangesets }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - name: Compose, version, and open the release PR
        id: version-pr
        uses: $/.github/actions/callisto-action
        with:
          setup_callisto: 'false'
          branch: main
          release_branch: callisto/version-packages
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

  release-candidate:
    name: Identify a merged Callisto release PR
    needs: [verify, version-pr]
    if: needs.version-pr.outputs.has_pending_changesets == 'false'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      is_release_pr: ${{ steps.candidate.outputs.is_release_pr }}
    steps:
      - id: candidate
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # This only schedules the job. `release plan` verifies the actual
          # parent-to-merge delta; labels and PR metadata are never authority.
          # The GitHub API check is complementary provenance evidence: a
          # trusted merge must be both an actual merge of the managed PR and
          # a GitHub-verified signed commit. It cannot be a direct push.
          prs=$(gh api --paginate "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${GITHUB_SHA}/pulls" --jq '[.[] | select(.merged_at != null and .base.ref == "main" and (.head.ref == "callisto/version-packages" or (.head.ref | test("^callisto/version-packages--[0-9a-f]{40}$"))))] | length')
          verified=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${GITHUB_SHA}" --jq '.commit.verification.verified')
          if [[ "$prs" == 1 && "$verified" == true ]]; then
            echo 'is_release_pr=true' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo 'is_release_pr=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  plan:
    name: Derive ephemeral intent from the merged release commit
    needs: release-candidate
    if: needs.release-candidate.outputs.is_release_pr == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - name: Derive and hash intent
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          callisto release plan --from-release-commit "$GITHUB_SHA" --decision .callisto/release-decision.json --out release-intent.json
          shasum -a 256 release-intent.json > release-intent.json.sha256
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: |
            release-intent.json
            release-intent.json.sha256
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 1

  build:
    name: Build the intent-bound source tree
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      attestations: write
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: extractions/setup-just@53165ef7e734c5c07cb06b3c8e7b647c5aa16db3 # v4.0.0
        with:
          just-version: '1.58.0'
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: .release-handoff
      - name: Verify handoff and build
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          (cd .release-handoff && shasum -a 256 -c release-intent.json.sha256)
          callisto release inspect --input .release-handoff/release-intent.json
          mkdir -p release-artifacts
          just build
      - name: Attest declared binary artifacts
        if: hashFiles('release-artifacts/**') != ''
        uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@4d101475d8b20a2381f78447822ac1eab6504dd8 # v4.2.2
        with:
          subject-path: release-artifacts/**
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: release-build
          path: |
            .release-handoff
            release-artifacts
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 1

  environment-policy:
    name: Verify release Environment protection
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      actions: read
    steps:
      - name: Require release Environment reviewers
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          reviewers=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/environments/release" --jq '.protection_rules // [] | map(select(.type == "required_reviewers")) | length')
          [[ "$reviewers" != 0 ]] || { echo '::error::GitHub Environment release has no required-reviewers protection rule'; exit 1; }

  execute:
    name: Execute approved release
    needs: environment-policy
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: release
    permissions:
      contents: write
      attestations: read
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: .release-intent
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-build
          path: .release-build
      - name: Verify same-run handoff before credentials
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          (cd .release-intent && shasum -a 256 -c release-intent.json.sha256)
          cmp .release-intent/release-intent.json .release-build/release-intent.json
      - name: Execute verified release
        env:
          CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
          NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
          TWINE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.TWINE_PASSWORD }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          state_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-release-state/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
          mkdir -p "$state_dir"
          args=(--intent .release-intent/release-intent.json --state "$state_dir/execution-state.json")
          if [[ -f .release-build/release-artifacts/manifest.json ]]; then
            args+=(--artifact-manifest .release-build/release-artifacts/manifest.json --artifact-dir .release-build/release-artifacts)
          fi
          callisto release execute "${args[@]}"

**Order the release PR's summary table and change list by severity, major first**

A reviewer merging a release PR is really answering one question: is anything breaking? Before this change, both the summary table and the "What's Changing" list rendered in plan order (roughly topological/declaration order), so a major bump could land anywhere among a dozen rows — a reviewer had to scan the whole table to be sure nothing was breaking, even though a major bump's own detail block already auto-opens.

Both the table and the change list are now sorted by severity descending (major, then minor, then patch/none), stable within each tier so otherwise-equal rows keep their original relative order. A breaking change is now always the first thing visible, in both places, regardless of where its package name or declaration would otherwise have put it.

content.text:
Found it, and it's a real, previously-undiscovered bug — not related to the PR-body work from earlier. Here's the root cause:

**What's actually happening:** Every release, `callisto version` bumps each crate's `version` field in `Cargo.toml` (e.g. `0.6.0` → `0.7.0`), but never regenerates `Cargo.lock`. `Cargo.lock` keeps recording those workspace members at their *old* version. Then, later in the pipeline, the "Derive ephemeral intent from the merged release commit" job checks out that release commit fresh and runs `cargo build` — and a plain `cargo build` silently rewrites `Cargo.lock` to fix the mismatch. That rewrite dirties the worktree, which trips the "release trust requires a clean worktree" check (error `E051`), and the whole run dies.

I reproduced it exactly: checked out the failing commit (`546f3df8`, PR #55) in an isolated worktree, ran `cargo build -p callisto-cli` just like CI does, and got ` M Cargo.lock` in `git status` afterward — a 10-line diff, every workspace member bumped `0.6.0` → `0.7.0`, nothing else.

The fix already exists in the codebase (`callisto version --refresh-lockfiles`, plumbed all the way through and documented in `ARCHITECTURE.md`'s "Lockfile Staleness" section) — it's just never been turned on for *this repo's own* release workflow, even though this repo has exactly the interdependent-Cargo-packages situation that flag exists for. Nobody wired it up.

**Fix applied** (in worktree `fix/release-pr-refresh-lockfiles`):
1. `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml` — pass `version_command: 'callisto version --refresh-lockfiles'` explicitly to the release action (scoped to this repo's own workflow, not the shared action's default, since that default is a public interface other consumers rely on and `cargo update --workspace` also touches third-party pins).
2. Regenerated `Cargo.lock` now, to unstick the currently-stuck release — verified a subsequent `cargo build` no longer dirties the tree.
3. Ran the release-action's 12-case contract suite: all pass.

`just ci-fast` is running now to confirm nothing else broke; I'll open the PR once it's green.

## Summary

The next job in the pipeline ("Derive ephemeral intent from the merged release commit") checks out that commit and runs a plain `cargo build`, which silently rewrites `Cargo.lock` to fix the mismatch — dirtying the worktree and tripping the release-trust clean-worktree check (`E051`).

Reproduced directly: checked out 546f3df8 in an isolated worktree, ran `cargo build -p callisto-cli` exactly as the job does, and got `M Cargo.lock` afterward (all 10 workspace members bumped 0.6.0 -> 0.7.0, nothing else).

release-intent.json.sha256
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 1

  build:
    name: Build the intent-bound source tree
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      attestations: write
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: extractions/setup-just@53165ef7e734c5c07cb06b3c8e7b647c5aa16db3 # v4.0.0
        with:
          just-version: '1.58.0'
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: .release-handoff
      - name: Verify handoff and build
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          (cd .release-handoff && shasum -a 256 -c release-intent.json.sha256)
          callisto release inspect --input .release-handoff/release-intent.json
          mkdir -p release-artifacts
          just build
      - name: Attest declared binary artifacts
        if: hashFiles('release-artifacts/**') != ''
        uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@4d101475d8b20a2381f78447822ac1eab6504dd8 # v4.2.2
        with:
          subject-path: release-artifacts/**
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: release-build
          path: |
            .release-handoff
            release-artifacts
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 1

  environment-policy:
    name: Verify release Environment protection
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      actions: read
    steps:
      - name: Require release Environment reviewers
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          reviewers=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/environments/release" --jq '.protection_rules // [] | map(select(.type == "required_reviewers")) | length')
          [[ "$reviewers" != 0 ]] || { echo '::error::GitHub Environment release has no required-reviewers protection rule'; exit 1; }

  execute:
    name: Execute approved release
    needs: environment-policy
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: release
    permissions:
      contents: write
      attestations: read
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: .release-intent
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-build
          path: .release-build
      - name: Verify same-run handoff before credentials
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          (cd .release-intent && shasum -a 256 -c release-intent.json.sha256)
          cmp .release-intent/release-intent.json .release-build/release-intent.json
      - name: Execute verified release
        env:
          CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
          NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
          TWINE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.TWINE_PASSWORD }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          state_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-release-state/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
          mkdir -p "$state_dir"
          args=(--intent .release-intent/release-intent.json --state "$state_dir/execution-state.json")
          if [[ -f .release-build/release-artifacts/manifest.json ]]; then
            args+=(--artifact-manifest .release-build/release-artifacts/manifest.json --artifact-dir .release-build/release-artifacts)
          fi
          callisto release execute "${args[@]}"

Pulling the actual release history (not just the one failed run) changes the picture significantly. Here's what's actually out of sync:

**1. This bug has silently blocked every release for ~2 weeks — confirmed, not speculative.**
crates.io's published `callisto-cli` is still at **0.5.0** (last published 2026-08-27). But `main` has already bumped to `0.6.0` and now `0.7.0` — meaning at least one full release cycle already merged its version-bump PR and then **never actually published**. I checked the prior release attempt (0.6.0, PR #51, run `34004467492`, 2026-09-06): it failed in the *exact same job* ("Derive ephemeral intent from the merged release commit") with a related error — `E124 ReleaseIntentStale: release intent no longer matches the current workspace snapshot`. Same job, same "fresh checkout → cargo build → re-derive/verify" shape, almost certainly the same Cargo.lock-drift trigger surfacing through a different validation layer (the error-taxonomy work in PRs #79-82 gave `ReleaseIntentStale` a real reason string later — before that it just failed silently-ish). This is very likely the actual answer to "why won't this work after weeks of fixes": the same untreated root cause (manifest/lockfile sync) has been resurfacing as different-looking errors each time, while the fixes so far improved diagnostics rather than removing the trigger.

**2. Confirmed OK, not a gap:** the `release` GitHub Environment has its required-reviewers protection rule properly configured (verified via API — you're the required reviewer).

**3. Unresolved, needs your input:** repo-level secrets are completely empty (`gh secret list` returns nothing), so `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`/`NPM_TOKEN`/`TWINE_PASSWORD` aren't set at the repo level. Since `execute` runs under `environment: release`, the token is probably scoped there instead (normal setup) — 0.5.0 did publish successfully at some point, so a token exists somewhere. I couldn't check environment-scoped secrets directly; the permission classifier blocked both `gh api .../environments/release/secrets` and `gh secret list --env release`. Worth a quick manual glance at repo Settings → Environments → release → Secrets before the next release attempt, just to rule it out.

**4. Unrelated, pre-existing, still open:** `just ci`/`ci-fast`'s `doc-check` stage is broken (bad rustdoc intra-doc link in `tag.rs`, introduced 2026-09-09). Doesn't gate CI or releases, but breaks local full-suite verification — you didn't answer yet whether you want this fixed.

Want me to (a) fix the `tag.rs` doc-check bug now, and (b) trace whether the 0.6.0 failure's exact `ReleaseIntentStale` code path shares the identical trigger with today's bug, for full certainty rather than "very likely"?

tasks:
  build:
    command: "cargo"
    args: ["build", "-p", "$project"]
    inputs:
      - "src/**/*"
      - "Cargo.toml"

    command: "cargo"
    args: ["test", "-p", "$project"]
    inputs:
      - "src/**/*"
      - "tests/**/*"
      - "Cargo.toml"
      - "**/*.snap"
      - "**/*.trycmd"

  lint:
    command: "cargo"

content.text:
I have enough to give you the substantive forward-look now; `just build` is still running in the background and I'll confirm it separately. Here's the actual risk map for phases that have **never once succeeded** under the current pipeline:

## Verified low-risk (checked the code, it's solid)
- **Crash-mid-publish resumability, Cargo path**: `dispatch_registry` classifies `cargo publish`'s "already exists"/"already uploaded" output as `AlreadyPublished` → `AlreadySatisfied`. Even though the execution-state file lives in `$RUNNER_TEMP` (wiped on every fresh runner, so it can't actually resume from a prior attempt), a from-scratch re-run safely re-derives progress by re-observing crates.io directly, rather than trusting stale local state.
- **Tag and GitHub-release creation**: both check "does this already exist and match?" before acting (`observed_tag`, `observed_forge_release_target`), and fail closed (not silently overwrite) on a mismatch.
- **Native binary artifacts**: `callisto matrix` currently returns `platformTargets: {}` for this workspace, so the `release-artifacts/` attestation step is a correct no-op right now, not a silent gap.
- **Environment protection**: confirmed live and correctly configured.

## Real, unaddressed gap
- **No propagation-lag handling for Cargo publishes.** npm has an explicit `RegistryPublishUnconfirmed` (E157) check — "npm reported published but the registry doesn't show it yet, re-run reconciliation, don't regenerate intent." Cargo has no equivalent. If crate N's publish succeeds but crates.io's index hasn't propagated by the time crate N+1 (which depends on N) tries to resolve it during `cargo publish --locked`'s verification build, that failure isn't specifically recognized — it falls into the generic `RegistryError::Other` bucket, and the whole `execute` job dies. It's very likely self-healing on a plain re-run (already-published crates get skipped via the idempotency check above), but it requires a human to notice and manually re-trigger `execute` rather than the pipeline retrying itself. Given crates.io's sparse index is normally fast, this is low-probability but exactly the kind of thing that would produce a confusing one-off failure on the very release that finally gets past `plan`.

## Still waiting on
`just build` (the exact command the `build` job runs — `moon run :build`, i.e. plain `cargo build -p $crate` for all 10 crates) is running now in the background; that job has also never succeeded once under this pipeline, so I want to confirm it actually completes clean before calling the rest of the pipeline sound.

callisto-graph: patch

**Confirm a Cargo publish landed on the registry before marking it done**

`dispatch_registry` only confirmed npm publishes against the registry after a successful publish call; Cargo went straight from "cargo publish exited 0" to `Published`, with no check that crates.io's index had actually caught up. If a dependent crate's publish ran before that propagation finished, its own `cargo publish --locked` verification build could fail to resolve the dependency, and the failure wouldn't be recognized as recoverable propagation lag.

Cargo publishes are now confirmed the same way npm's are: after a successful `cargo publish`, `cargo info <pkg>@<version>` must also confirm the registry shows it before the operation is marked `Published`. If it doesn't yet, the operation stays `Attempting` and reports `RegistryPublishUnconfirmed` -- re-running reconciliation once the registry catches up resolves it, with no need to regenerate the release intent.

PyPI's publish path has the same gap and is deliberately left open: this workspace has no PyPI package or credentials to verify a fix against.

## Summary

Stacked on #85 (that PR's commit shows up here too until it merges).

While auditing the rest of the release pipeline (build/execute have never run successfully under the current architecture -- every release attempt has died earlier, in `plan`), found that `dispatch_registry` confirms npm publishes against the registry after a successful publish call (`npm_version_is_published` + `RegistryPublishUnconfirmed`), but Cargo has no equivalent -- it goes straight from "`cargo publish` exited 0" to `Published`.

If a dependent crate's publish runs before crates.io's index has caught up on a sibling it depends on, that crate's own `cargo publish --locked` verification build can fail to resolve the dependency. That failure isn't recognized as recoverable propagation lag -- it just looks like a fresh, unrelated error mid-release.

- Cargo now confirms the same way npm does: after a successful `cargo publish`, `cargo info <pkg>@<version>` must also confirm the registry shows it before the operation is marked `Published`.
- If not yet visible, the operation stays `Attempting` and reports `RegistryPublishUnconfirmed` (E157) -- resolved by re-running reconciliation once the registry catches up, no release-intent regeneration needed.
- Generalized the E157 message/help text off npm-specific wording since it's now shared across ecosystems.
- Extracted the classification logic into a pure `classify_cargo_info_output` in `registry_argv.rs` (matching `classify_cargo_output`'s existing shape) so it's unit-testable without a full `ValidatedReleaseIntent` fixture.
- PyPI's publish path has the identical gap and is deliberately left open (noted in the changeset) -- no PyPI package or credentials in this workspace to verify a fix against.

content.text:
Confirmed — no retry wrapping exists anywhere in the workflow/action either. The CLI is the right place, for three concrete reasons:

1. **The retry needs registry-specific knowledge the shell doesn't have.** Confirming propagation means calling `cargo info`/`npm view` again and classifying its output (`classify_cargo_info_output`). That parsing logic already lives in Rust (`registry_argv.rs`) and is unit-tested there. Doing this in bash would mean re-implementing that same output classification a second time, in a second language, un-tested.

2. **Granularity.** The retry is scoped to exactly the thing that's flaky — "is this one just-published version visible yet" — not the whole `execute` command. If the retry lived at the GitHub Actions level instead (wrapping the whole `callisto release execute` step), any retry would re-run reconciliation from the top for every operation, not just poll the one lagging check. That's coarser and slower, even though the existing state-machine design (`AlreadySatisfied`) makes it *safe*.

3. **Testability.** Because it's a plain function with an injected `sleep` closure, the 4 tests verify the exact retry count and backoff schedule with zero real waiting. A bash-level retry loop would need to actually shell out and wait, or fake time at the OS/mock level — much weaker coverage.

One thing worth separating out: a **job-level** retry (retry the whole `execute` step in the GitHub Actions workflow, e.g. on any transient failure) is a legitimate, complementary idea — it'd cover failure classes this doesn't (a flaky runner, a `gh` CLI blip on the tag/forge-release steps), and the idempotent design I verified earlier (`AlreadySatisfied` checks for publish/tag/release) already makes that safe to add. But that's a different, broader mechanism than what you asked for — want me to look into that too, or is the in-process fix enough for now?

## Summary

Stacked on #86 (targets that branch, not main, to keep the diff scoped to just this change).

#86 added a registry-publish confirmation check for Cargo, matching npm's existing one -- but both check the registry exactly once. Propagation lag is normally sub-second, so a single check right after publish landing inside that window would fail immediately with `RegistryPublishUnconfirmed`, even though a moment later it would have succeeded on its own. As requested: up to 3 retries with fallback timing before actually failing.

- Retries up to 3 times (4 checks total) with exponential backoff: 2s, 4s, 8s (14s worst case).
- Only a registry-propagation miss is retried -- a hard error from the check itself (auth failure, network error) propagates immediately, no retry.
- `sleep` is injected as a plain closure (not a new trait/dependency threaded through the public API) so the new tests verify the exact retry count and backoff schedule with zero real wall-clock wait.

Based on the official Claude Code documentation, here's the precise answer:

## 1. **Interactive UI for Permission Rules**

Yes — use the `/permissions` command:
```bash
/permissions          # View current rules
/permissions edit     # Opens interactive rule editor
```

When auto mode is active, `/permissions edit` includes an **Auto mode** tab where you can add allow-rules without hand-editing JSON. You can also change the permission mode itself with **Shift+Tab** (in CLI/VS Code) or the mode selector (Desktop).

## 2. **Auto Mode vs. Allow-Rules**

**Critical distinction:** Auto mode's classifier and permission rules are *separate enforcement layers* that work **independently**. An allow-rule does *not* automatically bypass the auto-mode classifier. Instead:
- **Allow-rule** = permanent, persistent approval (saved to settings)
- **Classifier** = per-session decision by a second model evaluating "is this safe?"

The classifier will evaluate `gh pr merge` and `gh api` each time even if an allow-rule exists. To silence the auto-mode classifier on specific commands, you must also add them to the **auto mode classifier rules** (via the Auto mode tab in `/permissions edit`).

## 3. **Bash Rule Syntax**

The docs show Claude Code **strips shell wrappers and recognizes subcommands**, so:
- `Bash(gh pr merge *)` — matches `gh pr merge <n> --squash --admin` (with any flags)
- `Bash(gh api --method PUT *)` — matches `gh api --method PUT repos/.../rulesets/...` (with any trailing args)

However, **note the caveat:** rules match *each subcommand* in compound commands independently. For your two commands, you'd need:
```json
"permissions": {
  "allow": [
    "Bash(gh pr merge *)",
    "Bash(gh api --method PUT *)"
  ]
}
```

## 4. **Where the Rule Should Live**

For personal/machine-only rules that you don't want checked into the repo:
- **~/.claude/settings.json** (global, all projects)
- **.claude/settings.local.json** (project-local, git-ignored)

Do **not** put this in `.claude/settings.json` (the checked-in project file) unless the team wants it shared.

The docs explicitly state: "project's `.claude/settings.json` grant capability, so Claude Code applies them only after you accept the workspace trust dialog." Personal rules bypass that dialog.</result>

Let me check all `upload-artifact` usages for the same pattern before fixing.

name: Release

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: release-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  verify:
    name: Verify release candidate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Build local Callisto
        uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local

      - name: Install just
        uses: extractions/setup-just@53165ef7e734c5c07cb06b3c8e7b647c5aa16db3 # v4.0.0
        with:
          just-version: '1.58.0'

      - name: Format Check
        run: just fmt-check

      - name: Clippy Lints
        run: just lint

      - name: Install release verification tools
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@e67fa11c4b9316fa714ddf0abed07a0c3143b95b # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-nextest,ripgrep

      - name: Unit & Integration Tests
        run: just test

      - name: WASM Target Check
        run: just wasm-check

      - name: Install cargo-deny
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@e67fa11c4b9316fa714ddf0abed07a0c3143b95b # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-deny

      - name: Supply Chain Audit
        run: just audit

      - name: Reject mutable GitHub Actions references
        run: .github/tests/verify-action-pins.sh

  version-pr:
    name: Create or update the Callisto release PR
    needs: verify
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
    outputs:
      has_pending_changesets: ${{ steps.version-pr.outputs.hasChangesets }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - name: Compose, version, and open the release PR
        id: version-pr
        uses: $/.github/actions/callisto-action
        with:
          setup_callisto: 'false'
          branch: main
          release_branch: callisto/version-packages
          # This workspace bumps interdependent Cargo packages together, so a
          # bumped member's own Cargo.lock entry goes stale without this --
          # see ARCHITECTURE.md's "Lockfile Staleness" section.
          version_command: 'callisto version --refresh-lockfiles'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

  release-candidate:
    name: Identify a merged Callisto release PR
    needs: [verify, version-pr]
    if: needs.version-pr.outputs.has_pending_changesets == 'false'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      is_release_pr: ${{ steps.candidate.outputs.is_release_pr }}
    steps:
      - id: candidate
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # This only schedules the job. `release plan` verifies the actual
          # parent-to-merge delta; labels and PR metadata are never authority.
          # The GitHub API check is complementary provenance evidence: a
          # trusted merge must be both an actual merge of the managed PR and
          # a GitHub-verified signed commit. It cannot be a direct push.
          prs=$(gh api --paginate "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${GITHUB_SHA}/pulls" --jq '[.[] | select(.merged_at != null and .base.ref == "main" and (.head.ref == "callisto/version-packages" or (.head.ref | test("^callisto/version-packages--[0-9a-f]{40}$"))))] | length')
          verified=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${GITHUB_SHA}" --jq '.commit.verification.verified')
          if [[ "$prs" == 1 && "$verified" == true ]]; then
            echo 'is_release_pr=true' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo 'is_release_pr=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  plan:
    name: Derive ephemeral intent from the merged release commit
    needs: release-candidate
    if: needs.release-candidate.outputs.is_release_pr == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - name: Derive and hash intent
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          callisto release plan --from-release-commit "$GITHUB_SHA" --decision .callisto/release-decision.json --out release-intent.json
          shasum -a 256 release-intent.json > release-intent.json.sha256
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: |
            release-intent.json
            release-intent.json.sha256
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 1

  build:
    name: Build the intent-bound source tree
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      attestations: write
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: extractions/setup-just@53165ef7e734c5c07cb06b3c8e7b647c5aa16db3 # v4.0.0
        with:
          just-version: '1.58.0'
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: .release-handoff
      - name: Verify handoff and build
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          (cd .release-handoff && shasum -a 256 -c release-intent.json.sha256)
          callisto release inspect --input .release-handoff/release-intent.json
          mkdir -p release-artifacts
          just build
      - name: Attest declared binary artifacts
        if: hashFiles('release-artifacts/**') != ''
        uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@4d101475d8b20a2381f78447822ac1eab6504dd8 # v4.2.2
        with:
          subject-path: release-artifacts/**
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: release-build
          path: |
            .release-handoff
            release-artifacts
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 1

  environment-policy:
    name: Verify release Environment protection
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      actions: read
    steps:
      - name: Require release Environment reviewers
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          reviewers=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/environments/release" --jq '.protection_rules // [] | map(select(.type == "required_reviewers")) | length')
          [[ "$reviewers" != 0 ]] || { echo '::error::GitHub Environment release has no required-reviewers protection rule'; exit 1; }

  execute:
    name: Execute approved release
    needs: environment-policy
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: release
    permissions:
      contents: write
      attestations: read
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:

        with:
          name: release-build
          path: .release-build
      - name: Verify same-run handoff before credentials
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          (cd .release-intent && shasum -a 256 -c release-intent.json.sha256)
          cmp .release-intent/release-intent.json .release-build/release-intent.json
      - name: Execute verified release
        env:
          CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
          NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
          TWINE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.TWINE_PASSWORD }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          state_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-release-state/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
          mkdir -p "$state_dir"
          args=(--intent .release-intent/release-intent.json --state "$state_dir/execution-state.json")
          if [[ -f .release-build/release-artifacts/manifest.json ]]; then
            args+=(--artifact-manifest .release-build/release-artifacts/manifest.json --artifact-dir .release-build/release-artifacts)

name: Release

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: release-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  verify:
    name: Verify release candidate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Build local Callisto
        uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local

      - name: Install just
        uses: extractions/setup-just@53165ef7e734c5c07cb06b3c8e7b647c5aa16db3 # v4.0.0
        with:
          just-version: '1.58.0'

      - name: Format Check
        run: just fmt-check

      - name: Clippy Lints
        run: just lint

      - name: Install release verification tools
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@e67fa11c4b9316fa714ddf0abed07a0c3143b95b # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-nextest,ripgrep

      - name: Unit & Integration Tests
        run: just test

      - name: WASM Target Check
        run: just wasm-check

      - name: Install cargo-deny
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@e67fa11c4b9316fa714ddf0abed07a0c3143b95b # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-deny

      - name: Supply Chain Audit
        run: just audit

      - name: Reject mutable GitHub Actions references
        run: .github/tests/verify-action-pins.sh

  version-pr:
    name: Create or update the Callisto release PR
    needs: verify
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
    outputs:
      has_pending_changesets: ${{ steps.version-pr.outputs.hasChangesets }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - name: Compose, version, and open the release PR
        id: version-pr
        uses: $/.github/actions/callisto-action
        with:
          setup_callisto: 'false'
          branch: main
          release_branch: callisto/version-packages
          # This workspace bumps interdependent Cargo packages together, so a
          # bumped member's own Cargo.lock entry goes stale without this --
          # see ARCHITECTURE.md's "Lockfile Staleness" section.
          version_command: 'callisto version --refresh-lockfiles'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

  release-candidate:
    name: Identify a merged Callisto release PR
    needs: [verify, version-pr]
    if: needs.version-pr.outputs.has_pending_changesets == 'false'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      is_release_pr: ${{ steps.candidate.outputs.is_release_pr }}
    steps:
      - id: candidate
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # This only schedules the job. `release plan` verifies the actual
          # parent-to-merge delta; labels and PR metadata are never authority.
          # The GitHub API check is complementary provenance evidence: a
          # trusted merge must be both an actual merge of the managed PR and
          # a GitHub-verified signed commit. It cannot be a direct push.
          prs=$(gh api --paginate "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${GITHUB_SHA}/pulls" --jq '[.[] | select(.merged_at != null and .base.ref == "main" and (.head.ref == "callisto/version-packages" or (.head.ref | test("^callisto/version-packages--[0-9a-f]{40}$"))))] | length')
          verified=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${GITHUB_SHA}" --jq '.commit.verification.verified')
          if [[ "$prs" == 1 && "$verified" == true ]]; then
            echo 'is_release_pr=true' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo 'is_release_pr=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  plan:
    name: Derive ephemeral intent from the merged release commit
    needs: release-candidate
    if: needs.release-candidate.outputs.is_release_pr == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - name: Derive and hash intent
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          callisto release plan --from-release-commit "$GITHUB_SHA" --decision .callisto/release-decision.json --out release-intent.json
          shasum -a 256 release-intent.json > release-intent.json.sha256
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: |
            release-intent.json
            release-intent.json.sha256
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 1

  build:
    name: Build the intent-bound source tree
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      attestations: write
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: extractions/setup-just@53165ef7e734c5c07cb06b3c8e7b647c5aa16db3 # v4.0.0
        with:
          just-version: '1.58.0'
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: .release-handoff
      - name: Verify handoff and build
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          (cd .release-handoff && shasum -a 256 -c release-intent.json.sha256)
          callisto release inspect --input .release-handoff/release-intent.json
          mkdir -p release-artifacts
          just build
      - name: Attest declared binary artifacts
        if: hashFiles('release-artifacts/**') != ''
        uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@4d101475d8b20a2381f78447822ac1eab6504dd8 # v4.2.2
        with:
          subject-path: release-artifacts/**
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: release-build
          # include-hidden-files: upload-artifact excludes dotfiles by
          # default, and .release-handoff is one -- without this it silently
          # uploads nothing and "execute" downloads an empty artifact.
          include-hidden-files: true
          path: |
            .release-handoff
            release-artifacts
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 1

  environment-policy:
    name: Verify release Environment protection
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      actions: read
    steps:
      - name: Require release Environment reviewers
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          reviewers=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/environments/release" --jq '.protection_rules // [] | map(select(.type == "required_reviewers")) | length')
          [[ "$reviewers" != 0 ]] || { echo '::error::GitHub Environment release has no required-reviewers protection rule'; exit 1; }

  execute:
    name: Execute approved release
    needs: environment-policy
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: release
    permissions:
      contents: write
      attestations: read
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: .release-intent
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-build
          path: .release-build
      - name: Verify same-run handoff before credentials
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          (cd .release-intent && shasum -a 256 -c release-intent.json.sha256)
          cmp .release-intent/release-intent.json .release-build/release-intent.json
      - name: Execute verified release
        env:
          CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
          NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
          TWINE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.TWINE_PASSWORD }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          state_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-release-state/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
          mkdir -p "$state_dir"
          args=(--intent .release-intent/release-intent.json --state "$state_dir/execution-state.json")
          if [[ -f .release-build/release-artifacts/manifest.json ]]; then
            args+=(--artifact-manifest .release-build/release-artifacts/manifest.json --artifact-dir .release-build/release-artifacts)
          fi
          callisto release execute "${args[@]}"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Verify permissions that GitHub only enforces when a guarded release path is
# actually exercised. Keeping this separate from the generic action-pin check
# makes the release authority contract visible and testable on every PR.
set -euo pipefail

workflow=.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml

job_block() {
  local job="$1" next_job="$2"
  sed -n "/^  ${job}:$/,/^  ${next_job}:$/p" "$workflow"
}

require_line() {
  local block="$1" expected="$2" description="$3"
  if ! grep -Fqx "$expected" <<< "$block"; then
    printf 'release workflow contract failed: %s\n' "$description" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
}

version_pr="$(job_block version-pr release-candidate)"
require_line "$version_pr" '      contents: write' 'version-pr must write the managed branch'
require_line "$version_pr" '      pull-requests: write' 'version-pr must create or update the release PR'

release_candidate="$(job_block release-candidate plan)"
require_line "$release_candidate" '          prs=$(gh api --paginate "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${GITHUB_SHA}/pulls" --jq '\''[.[] | select(.merged_at != null and .base.ref == "main" and (.head.ref == "callisto/version-packages" or (.head.ref | test("^callisto/version-packages--[0-9a-f]{40}$"))))] | length'\'')' 'release-candidate must accept only canonical or SHA-suffixed managed branches'

build="$(job_block build environment-policy)"
require_line "$build" '      contents: read' 'build must read the intent-bound source tree'
require_line "$build" '      attestations: write' 'build must create provenance attestations'
require_line "$build" '      id-token: write' 'build must mint the Sigstore OIDC identity'

ci_workflow=.github/workflows/callisto-ci.yml
checkout_count=$(rg -n 'uses: actions/checkout@' "$ci_workflow" | wc -l)
credential_free_checkout_count=$(rg -n 'persist-credentials: false' "$ci_workflow" | wc -l)
if [[ "$checkout_count" != "$credential_free_checkout_count" ]]; then
  printf 'workflow contract failed: every Callisto CI checkout must disable persisted credentials\n' >&2
  exit 1
fi

require_line "$version_pr" '          persist-credentials: false' 'version-pr never git-pushes -- it commits through the forge API -- so it must not persist Git credentials'

if rg -U 'run: \|(?s:.*?)\$\{\{ inputs\.' .github/actions/setup-callisto/action.yml .github/actions/setup-callisto-wasm/action.yml > /dev/null; then
  printf 'workflow contract failed: composite-action inputs must enter shell through named environment variables\n' >&2
  exit 1
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Verify permissions that GitHub only enforces when a guarded release path is
# actually exercised. Keeping this separate from the generic action-pin check
# makes the release authority contract visible and testable on every PR.
set -euo pipefail

workflow=.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml

job_block() {
  local job="$1" next_job="$2"
  sed -n "/^  ${job}:$/,/^  ${next_job}:$/p" "$workflow"
}

require_line() {
  local block="$1" expected="$2" description="$3"
  if ! grep -Fqx "$expected" <<< "$block"; then
    printf 'release workflow contract failed: %s\n' "$description" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
}

version_pr="$(job_block version-pr release-candidate)"
require_line "$version_pr" '      contents: write' 'version-pr must write the managed branch'
require_line "$version_pr" '      pull-requests: write' 'version-pr must create or update the release PR'

release_candidate="$(job_block release-candidate plan)"
require_line "$release_candidate" '          prs=$(gh api --paginate "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${GITHUB_SHA}/pulls" --jq '\''[.[] | select(.merged_at != null and .base.ref == "main" and (.head.ref == "callisto/version-packages" or (.head.ref | test("^callisto/version-packages--[0-9a-f]{40}$"))))] | length'\'')' 'release-candidate must accept only canonical or SHA-suffixed managed branches'

build="$(job_block build environment-policy)"
require_line "$build" '      contents: read' 'build must read the intent-bound source tree'
require_line "$build" '      attestations: write' 'build must create provenance attestations'
require_line "$build" '      id-token: write' 'build must mint the Sigstore OIDC identity'

ci_workflow=.github/workflows/callisto-ci.yml
checkout_count=$(rg -n 'uses: actions/checkout@' "$ci_workflow" | wc -l)
credential_free_checkout_count=$(rg -n 'persist-credentials: false' "$ci_workflow" | wc -l)
if [[ "$checkout_count" != "$credential_free_checkout_count" ]]; then

fi

  printf 'workflow contract failed: composite-action inputs must enter shell through named environment variables\n' >&2
  exit 1
fi

"Build the intent-bound source tree" failed at its `upload-artifact` step: `No files were found with the provided path: .release-handoff / release-artifacts`, even though the download and build steps immediately before it both succeeded and `.release-handoff/release-intent.json` existed on disk at the time.

name: Release

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: release-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  verify:
    name: Verify release candidate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Build local Callisto
        uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local

      - name: Install just
        uses: extractions/setup-just@53165ef7e734c5c07cb06b3c8e7b647c5aa16db3 # v4.0.0
        with:
          just-version: '1.58.0'

      - name: Format Check
        run: just fmt-check

      - name: Clippy Lints
        run: just lint

      - name: Install release verification tools
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@e67fa11c4b9316fa714ddf0abed07a0c3143b95b # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-nextest,ripgrep

      - name: Unit & Integration Tests
        run: just test

      - name: WASM Target Check
        run: just wasm-check

      - name: Install cargo-deny
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@e67fa11c4b9316fa714ddf0abed07a0c3143b95b # v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-deny

      - name: Supply Chain Audit
        run: just audit

      - name: Reject mutable GitHub Actions references
        run: .github/tests/verify-action-pins.sh
